boundary_rationale: The part's opening annal notice, וַיִּפְשַׁ֤ע מוֹאָב֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַחֲרֵ֖י מ֥וֹת אַחְאָֽב, 'Moab rebelled against Israel after the death of Ahab,' shares no verb, actor, or vocabulary with what follows, and verse 2 pivots hard to a different subject and genre with וַיִּפֹּ֨ל אֲחַזְיָ֜ה, 'Ahaziah fell,' launching the sickbed inquiry that runs the rest of the chapter. A samekh follows 1:2 in the WLC (single-witness), dividing before v.3 and so favoring the very vv.1-2 grouping this row rejects; that mark is weak-tier corroboration only and cannot outweigh the total lexical disjunction between the two verses, but it belongs on the record rather than left silent. The rebellion notice itself is not resumed until 3:5's וַיִּפְשַׁ֥ע מֶֽלֶךְ מוֹאָ֖ב בְּמֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל, a verse standing outside this part that repeats 1:1's verb, its two nations, and its death-of-Ahab peg -- though Moab as a topic already re-enters the book one verse earlier, at 3:4's וּמֵישַׁ֥ע מֶֽלֶךְ מוֹאָ֖ב הָיָ֣ה נֹקֵ֑ד, the tribute notice that opens M8-2Kgs-008's own unit -- which reads 1:1 as a detached notice awaiting a later pickup rather than an orphaned one. The notice's own continuation belongs to Ahab's closing annals in the preceding book, a cross-book link noted here only as background, not argued as in-part evidence.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Grouping vv.1-2 as a joint scene-setting preface before the prophetic action starts at v.3 draws its only support from the samekh dividing after v.2, but it would still bind two subjects, a vassal kingdom's revolt and a king's household accident, that share no formula or wording at all.

boundary_rationale: Verse 2's royal initiative, וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח מַלְאָכִ֔ים, 'and he sent messengers' to Baal Zebub, draws the immediate counter-commission וּמַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֗ה דִּבֶּר֙ אֶל אֵלִיָּ֣ה, 'but the angel of Yahweh spoke to Elijah,' a disjunctive clause that starts the prophetic half of the legend at v.3; because this whole crisis originates with Ahaziah's own household in v.2, the row begins there rather than at the disconnected Moab notice. The three captain-of-fifty dispatches share one caption and the same fifty-man company sent three times rather than identical phrasing throughout: שַׂר חֲמִשִּׁ֖ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֑יו at v.9, שַׂר חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים אַחֵ֖ר וַחֲמִשָּׁ֑יו at v.11, and שַׂר חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים שְׁלִשִׁ֖ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֑יו at v.13; the wording drifts at each step  -- the dispatch clause of v.13 (וַיִּשְׁלַ֛ח שַׂר חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים) drops the אֵלָ֛יו object vv.9 and 11 carry, though the verse itself uses the pronoun twice later, at וַיִּתְחַנֵּ֤ן אֵלָיו֙ and וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלָ֔יו; v.11 alone swaps the ascent verb (וַיַּ֣עַל at 1:9, וַיַּ֡עַל at 1:13) for a bare 'answered,' and the content itself shifts from a king's command in vv.9 and 11 to a captain's plea for his life in v.13 -- yet the shared title, the repetition of that same fifty-man company (וַחֲמִשָּׁ֑יו constant at 1:9, 1:11, 1:13), sequenced by אַחֵ֖ר at v.11 and שְׁלִשִׁ֖ים at v.13, and above all the threefold death-sentence refrain, לֹֽא תֵרֵ֥ד מִמֶּ֖נָּה, repeated near-verbatim at 1:4, 1:6, and 1:16, still bind all three sendings into a single escalating triad rather than three scenes. A samekh sits after v.14 (single-witness), weakly marking the pivot from that triad into the angel's resolution at v.15 without turning it into a separate row, and the unit runs through Elijah's third face-to-face verdict at v.16, before v.17's annalistic notices take over.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the three fifty-man companies into three rows looks tempting given three separate royal dispatches, but all three share the same captain-of-fifty caption sent three times in strict sequence, so the triad reads as one legend's single escalation rather than three independent episodes even though the wording is not identical company to company.

boundary_rationale: Verse 17 pairs the fulfillment notice וַיָּ֜מָת כִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָ֣ה, 'and he died according to the word of Yahweh,' directly with the succession formula וַיִּמְלֹ֤ךְ יְהוֹרָם֙ תַּחְתָּ֔יו, 'and Jehoram reigned in his place,' inside a single verse, so the whole verse is kept together as one annalistic close rather than split between the legend and the reign notice. The Masoretic tradition records a petuchah at the end of v.17 as well as at the end of v.18 (both single-witness); the first sits exactly at the v.17/v.18 seam this row's own rejected alternative proposes, and disclosing only the mark that favors this row's own close would be one-sided. Neither mark can drive a boundary on its own, and the v.17 petuchah does not overturn what the grammar already decides: the succession clause shares its verse with the fulfillment clause and cannot be pried loose from it by any single-witness division. The row ends at v.18's boilerplate citation, הֲלֽוֹא הֵ֣מָּה כְתוּבִ֗ים עַל סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים, 'aren't they written in the book of the chronicles,' finishing Ahaziah's reign, right at the seam before chapter 2's unrelated itinerary narrative starts.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Ending the judgment legend at v.17 and starting the regnal notice at v.18 alone is the strongest rival, and it can now point to its own single-witness petuchah after v.17, yet it still fails because the succession clause sharing that same verse is formally part of the closing convention, not the legend, and a mark cannot split what the syntax binds.

boundary_rationale: Chapter 2 opens on its own incipit, וַיְהִ֗י בְּהַעֲל֤וֹת יְהוָה֙ אֶת אֵ֣לִיָּ֔הוּ בַּֽסְעָרָ֖ה הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם, 'and it happened, as Yahweh was about to take up Elijah in a whirlwind to heaven,' a temporal clause with none of the annalistic vocabulary of the reign notice just closed (the Masoretic tradition also marks a petuchah at the end of 1:18, single-witness, consistent with though not the basis for this break). Across four stations the same paired exchange recurs three times: Elijah's כִּ֤י יְהוָה֙ שְׁלָחַ֣נִי, 'for Yahweh has sent me,' at vv.2, 4, and 6, each met by Elisha's חַי יְהוָ֥ה וְחֵֽי נַפְשְׁךָ֖ אִם אֶעֶזְבֶ֑ךָּ, 'as Yahweh lives and as your soul lives, I will not leave you,' so Gilgal, Bethel, Jericho, and the Jordan crossing read as legs of a single itinerary rather than separate scenes. The arc closes with the search party's failed three-day hunt and Elisha's rebuke, הֲלֽוֹא אָמַ֥רְתִּי אֲלֵיכֶ֖ם אַל תֵּלֵֽכוּ, 'didn't I tell you, don't go,' at v.18, right before a new petitioner and setting open the following vignette.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Making each station its own row is the obvious-looking split given the location changes at Bethel, Jericho, and the Jordan, but the identical sent-me and will-not-leave-you exchange repeated at every stop marks continuous travel, not a new scene each time.

boundary_rationale: A new party and petition open this vignette: וַיֹּ֨אמְר֜וּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י הָעִיר֙ אֶל אֱלִישָׁ֔ע, 'the men of the city said to Elisha,' replacing the sons-of-the-prophets search party whose failed search just closed the ascension arc. The scene runs from that petition through the salt-and-spring sign-act to its own etiological close, וַיֵּרָפ֣וּ הַמַּ֔יִם עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה כִּדְבַ֥ר אֱלִישָׁ֖ע אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֵּֽר, 'so the waters were healed to this day, according to the word of Elisha,' at v.22, exactly where a petuchah marks the Masoretic division (single-witness) before a different cast and location open the next episode at v.23.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this healed-waters scene with the bears-at-Bethel episode into one accreditation complex is the nearest competing reading, but the two differ in location, cast, and closing device — a to-this-day fulfillment tag here against a bare travel notice there — so each keeps its own row.

boundary_rationale: A fresh scene opens on its own bare travel notice, וַיַּ֥עַל מִשָּׁ֖ם בֵּֽית אֵ֑ל, 'and he went up from there to Bethel,' a verse-initial wayyiqtol of motion introducing an entirely new cast within that same verse, וּנְעָרִ֤ים קְטַנִּים֙, 'young boys,' who never appeared in the healed-waters scene just closed; a petuchah closes that prior scene at 2:22 (single-witness), consistent with though not the basis for this break. The vignette runs through the mocking, the curse, and the mauling by bears, closing on the itinerary that carries Elisha onward, וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ מִשָּׁ֖ם אֶל הַ֣ר הַכַּרְמֶ֑ל and then וּמִשָּׁ֖ם שָׁ֥ב שֹׁמְרֽוֹן, 'and from there he returned to Samaria,' at v.25 — two itinerary notices rather than one — where the Masoretic tradition also places a petuchah (single-witness) at the very close of the chapter, again offered only as corroboration for an edge the travel-and-cast shift at v.23 and the itinerary at v.25 already carry unaided.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading vv.23-25 as the final leg of Elijah's ascension journey has some surface appeal since Elisha is still traveling from Jericho, but the paired commissioning-and-loyalty exchange binding that earlier arc never recurs here, and this episode has its own cast and its own closing notices.

boundary_rationale: Regnal accession formula opens this unit: וִיהוֹרָ֣ם בֶּן אַחְאָ֗ב מָלַ֤ךְ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּשֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן (oshb:2Kgs.3.1) names Jehoram, synchronizes him to Jehoshaphat's eighteenth year, and resumes the dynastic framework left dormant since ch. 2's frameless succession block. The unit ends where the evaluation clause of 3:3 gives way to an unrelated subject: 3:4 opens with a disjunctive clause, וּמֵישַׁ֥ע מֶֽלֶךְ מוֹאָ֖ב הָיָ֣ה נֹקֵ֑ד (oshb:2Kgs.3.4), introducing Mesha and Moab entirely outside the regnal-evaluation frame. A samekh sits after 3:3 in the WLC (oshb:2Kgs.3.3, samekh, single-witness) — weak corroboration, nothing more, for a seam the accession and rebellion notices have already drawn.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding 3:1-3 into the campaign that follows treats the accession formula as mere preamble, but the formula resists that reading on its own terms: וִיהוֹרָ֣ם בֶּן אַחְאָ֗ב מָלַ֤ךְ fronts the new king's name before the reign verb in a shape a targeted search finds nowhere else among the sixteen date-fronted accession openings (such as 8:16's וּבִשְׁנַ֣ת חָמֵ֗שׁ and 13:1's בִּשְׁנַ֨ת עֶשְׂרִ֤ים וְשָׁלֹשׁ֙) or the fifteen ben-N-years openings elsewhere in the book, so citing those two verses as formal twins to build a book-wide rule was unevidenced; what actually carries the seam is 3:1's own accession-and-synchronism content together with 3:4's disjunctive pivot to Mesha.

literature_type_guess: campaign_narrative_with_embedded_oracle (Moab rebellion and the water miracle)
boundary_rationale: Mesha's tribute notice opens the unit at 3:4, וּמֵישַׁ֥ע מֶֽלֶךְ מוֹאָ֖ב הָיָ֣ה נֹקֵ֑ד וְהֵשִׁ֤יב לְמֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ (oshb:2Kgs.3.4), a qatal-plus-participle clause continued by a weqatal, describing an occupation-and-tribute arrangement with no wayyiqtol anywhere in it; this fronted disjunction is the same construction decision M8-2Kgs-007 identifies as the turn away from the regnal evaluation, and it is what opens the new unit, not a report of revolt. The rebellion itself, and the chain's true wayyiqtol head, belongs to the next verse, וַיְהִ֖י כְּמ֣וֹת אַחְאָ֑ב וַיִּפְשַׁ֥ע מֶֽלֶךְ מוֹאָ֖ב בְּמֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:2Kgs.3.5), which resumes 1:1's own וַיִּפְשַׁ֤ע מוֹאָב֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַחֲרֵ֖י מ֥וֹת אַחְאָֽב in verb, participants, and temporal peg, giving this row's opening a positive cross-reference rather than a merely negative one. From 3:5's rebellion the wayyiqtol chain runs through the muster (וַיֵּצֵ֞א הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ יְהוֹרָ֛ם, oshb:2Kgs.3.6), the seven-day wilderness march, the water oracle, the crimson dawn, and the assault on Kir Hareseth, pausing only for circumstantial asides — וְלֹא הָיָ֨ה מַ֧יִם לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֛ה at 3:9, וְהִנֵּה מַ֥יִם בָּאִ֖ים מִדֶּ֣רֶךְ אֱד֑וֹם at 3:20, וְכָל מוֹאָב֙ שָֽׁמְע֔וּ at 3:21, וְהַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ זָרְחָ֣ה עַל הַמָּ֑יִם at 3:22, וְלֹ֥א יָכֹֽלוּ at 3:26 — no interior aside starts a new scene, since 3:21's Moabite muster (ending וַיַּעַמְד֖וּ עַֽל הַגְּבֽוּל) is the counter-view of one battle rather than an independent episode, before closing on the withdrawal notice וַיְהִ֥י קֶצֶף גָּד֖וֹל עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּסְעוּ֙ מֵֽעָלָ֔יו וַיָּשֻׁ֖בוּ לָאָֽרֶץ (oshb:2Kgs.3.27). Jehoshaphat's question at 3:11 (הַאֵ֨ין פֹּ֤ה נָבִיא֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה, oshb:2Kgs.3.11) is dialogue among kings who, per 3:12's וַיֵּרְד֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו מֶ֧לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל וִיהוֹשָׁפָ֖ט וּמֶ֥לֶךְ אֱדֽוֹם (oshb:2Kgs.3.12), relocate only as a single bloc to reach Elisha and never separate into distinct scenes, so the oracle remains an inset rather than a break of its own. A pe follows 3:27 in the WLC (oshb:2Kgs.3.27, pe, single-witness); it adds only weak-tier support to a close the withdrawal notice and the next vignette's cry-formula have already fixed.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating the consultation and oracle around 3:11-20 as a separate unit is the strongest competing reading, since it alone carries reported divine speech, but the three kings relocate together as one bloc at 3:12 and never separate from each other into independent scenes between the crisis and the battle, leaving nothing to hang a scene-break on.

boundary_rationale: A petition-cry formula launches this vignette apart from the campaign just concluded: וְאִשָּׁ֣ה אַחַ֣ת מִנְּשֵׁ֣י בְנֵֽי הַ֠נְּבִיאִים צָעֲקָ֨ה אֶל אֱלִישָׁ֜ע לֵאמֹ֗ר (oshb:2Kgs.4.1) brings forward an unnamed widow with no tie to Moab or the three kings. The crisis resolves at Elisha's instruction לְכִי֙ מִכְרִ֣י אֶת הַשֶּׁ֔מֶן וְשַׁלְּמִ֖י (oshb:2Kgs.4.7), sell the oil and settle the debt, immediately before 4:8 relocates everything with וַיְהִ֨י הַיּ֜וֹם וַיַּעֲבֹ֧ר אֱלִישָׁ֣ע אֶל שׁוּנֵ֗ם (oshb:2Kgs.4.8). A pe follows 4:7 in the WLC (oshb:2Kgs.4.7, pe, single-witness); the mark sits at weak-corroboration strength beside a boundary the cry-and-resolution formulas have already secured.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 4:1-7 as trailing off the Moab campaign fails because 3:27's own withdrawal notice, וַיְהִ֥י קֶצֶף גָּד֖וֹל עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּסְעוּ֙ מֵֽעָלָ֔יו וַיָּשֻׁ֖בוּ לָאָֽרֶץ (oshb:2Kgs.3.27), already closed the campaign before this chapter opens, and the widow, her sons, and her creditor share no participant or location with the war just concluded.

boundary_rationale: Elisha's regular route into Shunem opens the unit on a temporal formula, וַיְהִ֨י הַיּ֜וֹם וַיַּעֲבֹ֧ר אֱלִישָׁ֣ע אֶל שׁוּנֵ֗ם (oshb:2Kgs.4.8); that same וַיְהִ֨י הַיּ֜וֹם idiom recurs twice more inside this span, at 4:11's וַיְהִ֥י הַיּ֖וֹם וַיָּ֣בֹא שָׁ֑מָּה (oshb:2Kgs.4.11) and at 4:18's וַיְהִ֣י הַיּ֔וֹם וַיֵּצֵ֥א אֶל אָבִ֖יו (oshb:2Kgs.4.18), so the temporal idiom by itself cannot carry the opening seam; what actually opens the unit is 4:8's arrival clause together with the household entering the narrative for the first time, אִשָּׁ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֔ה. The hospitality-promise-death-raising sequence stays one continuous story bound by a repeated summons: קְרָ֖א לַשּׁוּנַמִּ֣ית הַזֹּ֑את (oshb:2Kgs.4.12) at the promise, קְרָא֙ אֶל הַשֻּׁנַמִּ֣ית הַזֹּ֔את (oshb:2Kgs.4.36) at the raising. It ends only when the mother physically leaves with her living son, וַתִּשָּׂ֥א אֶת בְּנָ֖הּ וַתֵּצֵֽא (oshb:2Kgs.4.37), just before 4:38 relocates the action again with וֶאֱלִישָׁ֞ע שָׁ֤ב הַגִּלְגָּ֨לָה֙ (oshb:2Kgs.4.38). A pe stands after 4:37 in the WLC (oshb:2Kgs.4.37, pe, single-witness), weak-tier support riding alongside the departure clause and Gilgal's relocation formula that actually mark this edge.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting the arc at the child's death (roughly 4:20) or at Gehazi's staff mission (4:29-31) is the standing temptation, but the errand is framed by the mother's refusal to leave Elisha and by Gehazi's failed report -- 4:30 closes וַיָּ֖קָם וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ אַחֲרֶֽיהָ, 4:31 opens וְגֵחֲזִ֞י עָבַ֣ר לִפְנֵיהֶ֗ם, and returns him with וַיָּ֤שָׁב לִקְרָאתוֹ֙ -- so the movement is internal to one continuous rescue rather than an arrival or departure that opens or closes a unit.

boundary_rationale: Famine at Gilgal opens its own scene, וֶאֱלִישָׁ֞ע שָׁ֤ב הַגִּלְגָּ֨לָה֙ וְהָרָעָ֣ב בָּאָ֔רֶץ (oshb:2Kgs.4.38), Elisha's return distinct from the Shunammite household just left behind. Three verses later the danger is neutralized, וְלֹ֥א הָיָ֛ה דָּבָ֥ר רָ֖ע בַּסִּֽיר (oshb:2Kgs.4.41), and a stranger enters with a different gift at 4:42, וְאִ֨ישׁ בָּ֜א מִבַּ֣עַל שָׁלִ֗שָׁה (oshb:2Kgs.4.42). A samekh follows 4:41 in the WLC (oshb:2Kgs.4.41, samekh, single-witness), offering the same weak-tier support while 4:42's stranger supplies the real evidence for this edge.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this with the loaves vignette that follows because both feed the sons of the prophets under famine ignores that each carries an independent arrival formula and a distinct object of danger, gourds against bread scarcity.

boundary_rationale: An outsider's arrival opens the part's final vignette, וְאִ֨ישׁ בָּ֜א מִבַּ֣עַל שָׁלִ֗שָׁה (oshb:2Kgs.4.42), a man bringing first-fruits bread distinct in gift and giver from the stew just purified. The part closes on the fulfillment device that recurs throughout the book, כִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָֽה (oshb:2Kgs.4.44), according to the word of Yahweh, sealing both this vignette and the assigned range together. A pe closes the WLC text at 4:44 (oshb:2Kgs.4.44, pe, single-witness), the weakest possible support for an edge that is otherwise fixed by the end of the assigned range itself.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 4:42-44 as a continuation of the pot vignette collapses two formula-marked scenes into one merely because both address hunger, but 4:42's opening construction, a fronted subject plus qatal, recurs at 4:1's וְאִשָּׁ֣ה אַחַ֣ת ... צָעֲקָ֨ה and at 4:38's וֶאֱלִישָׁ֞ע שָׁ֤ב; only 4:8's temporal וַיְהִ֨י הַיּ֜וֹם wayyiqtol breaks that shared pattern, so the fresh-arrival reading for 4:42 rests on the two openers it genuinely matches, 4:1 and 4:38, rather than on a claim about every vignette in the chapter.

boundary_rationale: The row opens at the part boundary with Naaman's formal narrator introduction, וְ֠נַעֲמָן שַׂר צְבָ֨א מֶֽלֶךְ אֲרָ֜ם הָיָ֣ה אִישׁ֩ גָּד֨וֹל (2Kgs.5.1), a disjunctive circumstantial clause built on a fronted subject plus the finite verb הָיָ֣ה, which recurs a second time in the same verse's וְהָאִ֗ישׁ הָיָ֛ה גִּבּ֥וֹר חַ֖יִל מְצֹרָֽע; this exposition launches the whole healing complex and carries the letter frame of 5.5-7 and the Jordan dialogues as one unbroken scene. It closes at Elisha's dismissal formula לֵ֣ךְ לְשָׁל֑וֹם and Naaman's departure notice וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ מֵאִתּ֖וֹ כִּבְרַת אָֽרֶץ (2Kgs.5.19); 5.20 opens a new scene on Gehazi, but that verse begins with the ordinary wayyiqtol וַיֹּ֣אמֶר גֵּיחֲזִ֗י נַעַר֮ אֱלִישָׁ֣ע אִישׁ הָאֱלֹהִים֒, its subject trailing the verb rather than fronted as at 5.1, so the edge rests on Naaman's exit notice and the shift of the acting party rather than on any matching syntax between the two verses. The samekh recorded after MT 5.19 (single-witness) offers only weak corroboration here, and the row treats the mid-verse tension between Elisha's speech and Naaman's exit notice as internal to 5.19 rather than as a seam in its own right.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The strongest competing reading keeps all twenty-seven verses as a single Naaman-Gehazi diptych bound by shared moral irony, but it must yield to Naaman's own exit notice at the close of 5.19 together with 5.20's full-title reintroduction of Gehazi, which jointly reopen the account on new ground even though 5.20's clause is an ordinary wayyiqtol rather than a fronted construction matching 5.1.

boundary_rationale: The unit begins at 5.20's actual opening word, וַיֹּ֣אמֶר גֵּיחֲזִ֗י נַעַר֮ אֱלִישָׁ֣ע אִישׁ הָאֱלֹהִים֒, an ordinary wayyiqtol clause with the subject trailing the verb rather than a fronted construction, which reintroduces the servant by his full office and turns attention onto his own master's household; the topical echo of 5.1's introduction of Naaman by full title is real, but the two clauses are not syntactic twins, since 5.1 fronts its subject before a finite הָיָ֣ה and 5.20 does not. What actually opens this scene is the departure notice closing 5.19, וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ מֵאִתּ֖וֹ כִּבְרַת אָֽרֶץ, together with the wholesale turnover of the acting party from Naaman to Gehazi. The unit ends with the transferred-disease verdict וְצָרַ֤עַת נַֽעֲמָן֙ תִּֽדְבַּק בְּךָ֔ and the closing tableau וַיֵּצֵ֥א מִלְּפָנָ֖יו מְצֹרָ֥ע כַּשָּֽׁלֶג (2Kgs.5.27), a reversal notice that inverts Naaman's own cleansing. MT records a samekh after 5.27 (single-witness), sitting atop a formula already sufficient on its own, and the modern chapter division that follows is metadata only.
strongest_rejected_alternative: One could isolate Gehazi's chase and deceit (5.20-24) from his sentencing (5.25-27) at his return, but 5.25's circumstantial וְהוּא בָא֙ וַיַּעֲמֹ֣ד אֶל אֲדֹנָ֔יו is a dialogue turn inside one continuous exposure scene, not a fresh participant tag.

boundary_rationale: This short vignette opens at 6.1's clause-initial wayyiqtol, וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ בְנֵֽי הַנְּבִיאִ֖ים אֶל אֱלִישָׁ֑ע, the sons of the prophets addressing Elisha about crowded quarters; unlike 4.1's genuinely fronted וְאִשָּׁ֣ה אַחַ֣ת מִנְּשֵׁ֣י בְנֵֽי הַ֠נְּבִיאִים צָעֲקָ֨ה, this clause carries no disjunction of its own, so the seam here rests instead on 5.27's terminal reversal tableau, וַיֵּצֵ֥א מִלְּפָנָ֖יו מְצֹרָ֥ע כַּשָּֽׁלֶג, together with the wholly different participant set and problem, a building project rather than a household reckoning, that 6.1 brings on. It closes with the resolution clause וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח יָד֖וֹ וַיִּקָּחֵֽהוּ (2Kgs.6.7), the recovered axe head now in hand, and MT records a pe immediately after 6.7 (single-witness), weakly corroborating the edge before 6.8 opens an unrelated war council.
strongest_rejected_alternative: This vignette could be folded forward into the following raid narrative since both feature Elisha among Arameans, but 6.8 introduces the king of Aram's council as an entirely new subject facing a military rather than domestic problem, so the tool-recovery scene must close first.

boundary_rationale: The raid narrative opens on a disjunctive background clause, וּמֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָ֔ם הָיָ֥ה נִלְחָ֖ם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (2Kgs.6.8), waw-subject-qatal-participle installing a fresh scene-initiating subject in a durative state of war rather than a recurring council device — the verse's own council verb, וַיִּוָּעַץ֙, is unique in the book, so no repeated formula actually exists for that word to name. Its many internal movements, the Dothan siege, the servant's opened eyes, the march into Samaria, run as continuous scene-flow without any renewed disjunctive fronted-subject clause: two figures do enter partway through by ordinary wayyiqtol, וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אַחַ֣ד מֵֽעֲבָדָ֔יו at 6.12 and וַ֠יַּשְׁכֵּם מְשָׁרֵ֨ת אִ֥ישׁ הָֽאֱלֹהִים֮ at 6.15, but neither clause is fronted or disjunctive, so both remain internal to the one continuous Dothan scene rather than opening fresh units. The arc closes on a cessation notice rather than an etiological one, since וְלֹֽא יָ֤סְפוּ עוֹד֙ גְּדוּדֵ֣י אֲרָ֔ם לָב֖וֹא בְּאֶ֥רֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (2Kgs.6.23) carries none of the book's עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה refrain and simply reports that the raiding stopped, corroborated only weakly by MT's pe recorded after 6.23 (single-witness).
strongest_rejected_alternative: A stronger candidate than splitting the twin prayer verses 6.17/6.18 — which plainly belong to one uninterrupted blindness-and-guidance sequence — is the Samaria-arrival clause at 6.19b-20, וַיְהִי֮ כְּבֹאָ֣ם שֹׁמְרוֹן֒, an explicit change of location; it still fails as an independent seam, since it is the direct payoff of the deception Elisha launches at 6:19a and of the march reported at the close of that same verse (וַיֹּ֥לֶךְ אוֹתָ֖ם שֹׁמְרֽוֹנָה), rather than an arrival formula opening anything new.

boundary_rationale: The complex opens on the temporal transition וַֽיְהִי֙ אַחֲרֵי כֵ֔ן, immediately followed by the muster clause וַיִּקְבֹּ֛ץ בֶּן הֲדַ֥ד מֶֽלֶךְ אֲרָ֖ם אֶת כָּל מַחֲנֵ֑הוּ וַיַּ֕עַל וַיָּ֖צַר עַל שֹׁמְרֽוֹן (oshb:2Kgs.6.24); the transition marker itself signals the fresh unit, with the muster verb supplying its content, so the near edge rests on both words rather than skipping past the marker to the verb alone. The ascend-and-besiege pair וַיַּ֕עַל וַיָּ֖צַר recurs in consonantal form at 17:5, with different accentuation and with the object noun standing between the two verbs, where 6:24 has them contiguous (וַיַּ֨עַל֙ שֹׁמְר֔וֹן וַיָּ֥צַר עָלֶ֖יהָ), a genuine lexical echo the book strategy's own device matrix groups with this verse under one campaign-muster/siege category; 3:6's departure-and-levy pair (וַיֵּצֵ֞א הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ ... וַיִּפְקֹ֖ד אֶת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל) belongs to that same functional family without matching this verse's wording, and is better named a troop-levy opener than called an identical siege-muster shape. The complex closes twenty-nine verses later on וַיְהִי ל֖וֹ כֵּ֑ן וַיִּרְמְס֨וּ אֹת֥וֹ הָעָ֛ם בַּשַּׁ֖עַר וַיָּמֹֽת (oshb:2Kgs.7.20), the verdict on the skeptical captain whose doubt was first voiced as הִנְּכָ֤ה רֹאֶה֙ בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ וּמִשָּׁ֖ם לֹ֥א תֹאכֵֽל (oshb:2Kgs.7.2) and restated at 7:19 as הִנְּךָ֤ רֹאֶה֙ בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ וּמִשָּׁ֖ם לֹ֥א תֹאכֵֽל, a doubt-and-verdict inclusio binding the famine, threat, lepers, and discovery scenes into one argument. Samekh marks after 6:33 and 7:2 (oshb, single-witness) sit at internal turns inside this argument, while the samekh after 7:20 (oshb, single-witness) weakly corroborates the closing edge, in every case corroboration only and never the driver.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The nearest rival split falls just before the disjunctive וְאַרְבָּעָ֧ה אֲנָשִׁ֛ים הָי֥וּ מְצֹרָעִ֖ים פֶּ֣תַח הַשָּׁ֑עַר (7:3), where four new participants appear at a fixed location, but that seam would separate the doubt-oracle from its fulfillment and unravel the inclusio the whole complex depends on.

boundary_rationale: The Shunammite's return opens on a disjunctive vav-subject-qatal clause rather than the mainline narrative chain: וֶאֱלִישָׁ֡ע דִּבֶּ֣ר אֶל הָאִשָּׁה֩ אֲשֶׁר הֶחֱיָ֨ה אֶת בְּנָ֜הּ (oshb:2Kgs.8.1), a grammatical flashback marker pulling the reader back before the famine years just narrated. The audience resolves at הָשֵׁ֤יב אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר לָהּ֙ וְאֵת֙ כָּל תְּבוּאֹ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה מִיּ֛וֹם עָזְבָ֥ה אֶת הָאָ֖רֶץ וְעַד עָֽתָּה (oshb:2Kgs.8.6), the king's restoration order answering her petition, immediately before the next unit opens on the flat location shift וַיָּבֹ֤א אֱלִישָׁע֙ דַּמֶּ֔שֶׂק (oshb:2Kgs.8.7). Elisha and the unnamed king of Israel do recur as background figures on both flanks -- Elisha sitting at home at 6:32 (וֶאֱלִישָׁע֙ יֹשֵׁ֣ב בְּבֵית֔וֹ) and speaking at 7:1 (וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלִישָׁ֔ע), then arriving at Damascus at 8:7; the king walking the wall at 6:26 -- so the row's isolation cannot rest on participant identity; what is unique to this scene is the petitioner herself, the specific royal audience she is granted, and the land-restitution subject matter, none of which the siege complex or the Damascus scene shares.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The likeliest rival treats 8:1-6 as a trailing coda to the siege complex, but that reading fails since the disjunctive opener at 8:1 marks a backward temporal jump rather than a continuation, and the complex it would extend already closed on its own fulfillment formula at 7:20.

boundary_rationale: Elisha's arrival at Damascus opens the scene with an explicit location and circumstance shift, וַיָּבֹ֤א אֱלִישָׁע֙ דַּמֶּ֔שֶׂק וּבֶן הֲדַ֥ד מֶֽלֶךְ אֲרָ֖ם חֹלֶ֑ה (oshb:2Kgs.8.7), pairing a new place with Ben-hadad's illness as the occasion for Hazael's embassy. It closes on the regicide-succession pattern shared with Israel's and Judah's own reign notices, וַיִּמְלֹ֥ךְ חֲזָהאֵ֖ל תַּחְתָּֽיו (oshb:2Kgs.8.15), spoken immediately after the smothering that fulfills Elisha's earlier tears. Between arrival and succession the errand does move -- Ben-hadad addresses Hazael directly at 8:8 (וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶל חֲזָהאֵ֗ל), Hazael leaves Elisha's presence for his master's at 8:14 (וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ מֵאֵ֣ת אֱלִישָׁ֗ע וַיָּבֹא֙ אֶל אֲדֹנָ֔יו), and a fresh day opens at the sickbed with וַיְהִ֣י מִֽמָּחֳרָ֗ת at 8:15 -- but these are turn-markers inside one continuous commissioned errand rather than scene breaks, since none of them carries a regnal-year date formula, a commissioned dispatch of a prophet, or an arrival at a new named place -- conceding וַיְהִ֣י מִֽמָּחֳרָ֗ת at 8:15 as a temporal frame subordinated to an errand already under way, and that 8:8's dispatch-to-inquire parallels 1:2's construction without itself opening a scene.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at Hazael's 8:14 departure back to his master remains the nearest rival seam, but it fails for the same reason the interior turn-markers do generally: the verse carries no regnal-year date formula, commissioned dispatch, or arrival at a new named place, only a change of addressee inside one embassy.

boundary_rationale: Jehoram of Judah's frame opens with the standard synchronism-plus-accession formula וּבִשְׁנַ֣ת חָמֵ֗שׁ לְיוֹרָ֤ם בֶּן אַחְאָב֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וִיהוֹשָׁפָ֖ט מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה מָלַ֛ךְ יְהוֹרָ֥ם בֶּן יְהוֹשָׁפָ֖ט מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:2Kgs.8.16). It closes on the paired source-citation and death-succession formulas הֲלֽוֹא הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:2Kgs.8.23) and וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אֲחַזְיָ֥הוּ בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו (oshb:2Kgs.8.24). The Edom-and-Libnah notice in between carries its own report formula, בְּיָמָיו֙ פָּשַׁ֣ע אֱד֔וֹם (oshb:2Kgs.8.20), but supplies neither an accession year nor a source citation, so it remains an episode reported inside the reign rather than a break in it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating the Edom-and-Libnah notice (8:20-22) as its own row is the natural temptation given its report formula, but it loses because nothing in 8:20 marks a reign boundary — the citation and succession formula that actually close the unit arrive only after the notice, folding it into Jehoram's frame.

boundary_rationale: Ahaziah of Judah's reign opens on its own regnal dating notice, synchronized to Joram's year and stamped with the accession verb, בִּשְׁנַת֙ שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה לְיוֹרָ֥ם בֶּן אַחְאָ֖ב מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מָלַ֛ךְ אֲחַזְיָ֥הוּ בֶן יְהוֹרָ֖ם מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:2Kgs.8.25), followed by the age formula and the Ahab-house evaluation at 8:26-27. This unit has no closing or source-citation formula inside the present part: the Ramoth-gilead engagement itself is narrated at וַיֵּ֜לֶךְ אֶת יוֹרָ֣ם בֶּן אַחְאָ֗ב לַמִּלְחָמָ֛ה עִם חֲזָהאֵ֥ל מֶֽלֶךְ אֲרָ֖ם בְּרָמֹ֣ת גִּלְעָ֑ד, closing with the wounding clause וַיַּכּ֥וּ אֲרַמִּ֖ים אֶת יוֹרָֽם (oshb:2Kgs.8.28), and the row runs on into Joram's withdrawal to recover from it, וַיָּשָׁב֩ יוֹרָ֨ם הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לְהִתְרַפֵּ֣א בְיִזְרְעֶ֗אל מִן הַמַּכִּים֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יַכֻּ֤הוּ אֲרַמִּים֙ בָּֽרָמָ֔ה (oshb:2Kgs.8.29). The far edge does sit before a genuine internal opener rather than a bare external cut: 9:1 begins וֶאֱלִישָׁע֙ הַנָּבִ֔יא קָרָ֕א לְאַחַ֖ד מִבְּנֵ֣י הַנְּבִיאִ֑ים, the same vav-fronted-subject-qatal pattern that independently opens new Elisha pericopes at 4:38 and 13:14 and that this cluster's own 8:1 decision already treats as decisive; but the campaign's fixed part boundary still requires this row to end at 8:29, so the row honestly discloses a suspension rather than claiming the seam is purely an artefact of that boundary. The single-witness pe cited at 8:29 (oshb, single-witness) falls exactly at this disclosed suspension point, and the book strategy's own notes independently flag this same wound material as resumed later by a Wiederaufnahme once the Jehu narrative opens at 9:15.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the row to fold in 9:1 -- since that verse's fronted-subject-qatal opener genuinely marks a fresh Elisha scene rather than a mere external cutpoint -- is the nearest rival, but the campaign's fixed part boundary forecloses it regardless of that formula's strength, so the row still ends at 8:29 with the wound disclosed rather than resolved.

boundary_rationale: The unit opens on Elisha's own fronted-subject introduction, וֶאֱלִישָׁע֙ הַנָּבִ֔יא קָרָ֕א לְאַחַ֖ד מִבְּנֵ֣י הַנְּבִיאִ֑ים (oshb:2Kgs.9.1), the identical vav-subject-qatal construction that opens fresh Elisha scenes at 4:38 (וֶאֱלִישָׁ֞ע שָׁ֤ב הַגִּלְגָּ֨לָה֙) and 13:14 (וֶֽאֱלִישָׁע֙ חָלָ֣ה), with the commissioning imperative חֲגֹ֣ר מָתְנֶ֗יךָ that follows serving as the errand's content rather than its opening signal. It closes on the acclamation and trumpet blast, וַֽיִּתְקְעוּ֙ בַּשּׁוֹפָ֔ר וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ מָלַ֥ךְ יֵהֽוּא (oshb:2Kgs.9.13), a public proclamation answering the private anointing of 9:6. The very next clause pivots to a fresh conspiracy verb, וַיִּתְקַשֵּׁ֗ר יֵה֛וּא (oshb:2Kgs.9.14), signaling that the insurrection proper begins a new movement -- a shift from a lone prophet's secret errand under a scene-opening formula to an armed captain's public conspiracy, not merely a change of pace.
strongest_rejected_alternative: One could fold this commissioning scene into the killing scene that follows as a single 'Jehu becomes king' arc, but 9:14's conspiracy verb opens a mode the fronted-subject formula at 9:1 never shares, so the public/private divide holds as a genuine seam.

literature_type_guess: coup_narrative (Jezreel chariot pursuit and double regicide)
boundary_rationale: The scene launches on the conspiracy verb itself, וַיִּתְקַשֵּׁ֗ר יֵה֛וּא בֶּן יְהוֹשָׁפָ֥ט בֶּן נִמְשִׁ֖י אֶל יוֹרָ֑ם (oshb:2Kgs.9.14), then immediately resumes Joram's Ramoth wound in a Wiederaufnahme, וַיָּשָׁב֩ יְהוֹרָ֨ם הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לְהִתְרַפֵּ֣א בִיְזְרְעֶ֗אל (oshb:2Kgs.9.15) -- a continuity device that hands the reader back into the chariot-pursuit action rather than opening fresh ground. The pursuit itself is not confined to Jezreel: Ahaziah's own flight is introduced by a fronted-subject-qatal clause, וַאֲחַזְיָ֤ה מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָה֙ רָאָ֔ה וַיָּ֕נָס (oshb:2Kgs.9.27), and carries the action out to Megiddo and on to burial in Jerusalem; that clause and the watchman relays opening at 9:17 (וְהַצֹּפֶה֩ עֹמֵ֨ד, oshb:2Kgs.9.17) are internal turn-markers tested against a seam here and rejected, since neither carries its own conspiracy, date, or messenger formula reopening a new scene, rather than proof that nothing at all interrupts one unbroken drive. The unit is closed instead by a dated regnal notice, וּבִשְׁנַת֙ אַחַ֣ת עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה לְיוֹרָ֖ם בֶּן אַחְאָ֑ב מָלַ֥ךְ אֲחַזְיָ֖ה עַל יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:2Kgs.9.29), which is the book's ordinary bi-shnat accession formula in shape -- the same bi-shnat accession construction that opens the reign accounts at 8:16 and 8:25 -- but functions here as a retrospective synchronism recorded only once both kings are dead, so no reign follows it and it cannot open anything; the single-witness pe actually falls one verse earlier, after 9:28 (oshb, single-witness), a placement disclosed here rather than silently passed over.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A finer cut could isolate the watchman exchanges (9:17-22) as their own vignette, but each relay only advances the same approaching chariot without any scene-opening formula of its own -- exactly the turn-marker pattern this campaign rules against splitting.

boundary_rationale: A fresh arrival notice reintroduces the subject and brings in an entirely new interlocutor at once: וַיָּב֥וֹא יֵה֖וּא יִזְרְעֶ֑אלָה וְאִיזֶ֣בֶל שָׁמְעָ֗ה (9:30), Jezebel now painting her eyes for a confrontation the previous unit never touched. The scene ends on an explicit citation formula naming its source, וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ דְּבַר יְהוָ֣ה ה֔וּא אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֗ר בְּיַד עַבְדּ֛וֹ אֵלִיָּ֥הוּ הַתִּשְׁבִּ֖י (9:36), carried through the dung-on-the-field image at 9:37, where a petuchah follows in the WLC (oshb:2Kgs.9.37, single-witness) — weak corroboration only, but it sits exactly where the citation formula has already closed the account. Nothing in the intervening dialogue (the eunuchs, the burial party) reopens participants from the prior chariot scene.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Some would keep Jehu's entry to Jezreel (9:30) attached to the pursuit ending at 9:29, treating it as that same journey's final stop, but the repeated arrival verb plus Jezebel's wholly fresh toilette and speech mark this as its own scene rather than a mere coda.

literature_type_guess: coup_narrative (letter-driven massacre of Ahab's seventy sons)
boundary_rationale: This unit opens on the disjunctive verbless clause about Ahab's household, וּלְאַחְאָ֛ב שִׁבְעִ֥ים בָּנִ֖ים בְּשֹׁמְר֑וֹן (oshb:2Kgs.10.1), setting the scene before the letter frame proper begins, וַיִּכְתֹּב֩ יֵה֨וּא סְפָרִ֜ים וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח שֹׁמְר֗וֹן, which then organizes the unit's action rather than opening it. Its resolution stacks Jehu's own speech, in which he voices the fulfillment claim to the assembled people, דְּע֣וּ אֵפ֗וֹא כִּי֩ לֹ֨א יִפֹּ֜ל מִדְּבַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אַ֔רְצָה אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה עַל בֵּ֣ית אַחְאָ֑ב (oshb:2Kgs.10.10), against the narrator's own completion clause, עַד בִּלְתִּ֥י הִשְׁאִֽיר ל֖וֹ שָׂרִֽיד (oshb:2Kgs.10.11), so the row's close pairs a character's fulfillment claim with the narrator's confirming report rather than two notices of the same register. The second letter (10:6) and the head-baskets (10:7-8) stay inside this frame as its own internal turns, never independent units, and the row hands off cleanly to the triple movement verb opening 10:12.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The strongest rival reading binds 10:1-17 into one seventeen-verse fulfillment chain, but Jehu's own departure at 10:12 -- a fresh triple movement verb toward a named destination -- is exactly the location change this campaign flags for seam-testing, and it holds up under scrutiny.

literature_type_guess: coup_narrative (Beth-eked kinsmen slaughter and Samaria purge)
boundary_rationale: A triple movement verb reopens the narrative on the road: וַיָּ֨קָם֙ וַיָּבֹ֔א וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ שֹׁמְר֑וֹן (oshb:2Kgs.10.12), placing Jehu at the shearing house before any letter reaches there, a clean location shift from the Jezreel purge just finished. The samekh after 10:14 (oshb, single-witness) falls between the forty-two kinsmen's slaughter and the Jehonadab encounter, and the verse just past it does open with its own departure formula, וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ מִשָּׁ֡ם וַיִּמְצָ֣א אֶת יְהוֹנָדָב֩ (oshb:2Kgs.10.15) -- the same departure construction, pointed מִשָּׁ֖ם at 2:25 and מִשָּׁ֡ם at 10:15 -- but here it marks a station inside the single journey already announced at 10:12 and only consummated at 10:17's וַיָּבֹא֙ שֹֽׁמְר֔וֹן, not an independent scene of its own. The unit closes where Ahab's remaining household in Samaria is struck down עַד הִשְׁמִיד֑וֹ כִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֶּ֖ר אֶל אֵלִיָּֽהוּ (oshb:2Kgs.10.17), reinforced by a petuchah at that verse (oshb, single-witness).
strongest_rejected_alternative: The genuine departure formula at 10:15 tempts a split between the kinsmen episode and the Jehonadab-to-Samaria sequence, but the destination announced already at 10:12 and only reached at 10:17 outranks it: Jehonadab boards Jehu's chariot mid-journey toward a goal the text has already named, so the local departure is a way-station, not a new opening.

boundary_rationale: Jehu's assembly summons opens the ruse on its own footing, וַיִּקְבֹּ֤ץ יֵהוּא֙ אֶת כָּל הָעָ֔ם (oshb:2Kgs.10.18), a muster distinct in both addressee and purpose from the household purge just concluded at Samaria. The account is capped by a summary wayyiqtol taking the national object אֶת הַבַּ֖עַל as its object, with the ablative מִיִּשְׂרָאֵֽל marking a national scope, וַיַּשְׁמֵ֥ד יֵה֛וּא אֶת הַבַּ֖עַל מִיִּשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:2Kgs.10.28); 10:17 had already closed the household purge with the same hiphil root over a named object, עַד הִשְׁמִיד֑וֹ (oshb:2Kgs.10.17), so what actually distinguishes 10:28 is that ablative national scope, absent from 10:17. The wardrobe-keeper notice at 10:22 (לַֽאֲשֶׁר֙ עַל הַמֶּלְתָּחָ֔ה), the eighty guards at 10:24, and the latrine notice at 10:27 are all internal stages of this single stratagem, never separate scenes.
strongest_rejected_alternative: One could carry the unit forward into 10:29-31 on the thread of Jehu's religious zeal, but the adversative רַ֠ק opening 10:29 pivots from narrated action to evaluative commentary on an unrelated failure (the Jeroboam calves), a register change the summary verdict at 10:28 has already closed off.

boundary_rationale: The adversative particle רַ֠ק חֲטָאֵ֞י יָרָבְעָ֤ם בֶּן נְבָט֙ (oshb:2Kgs.10.29) turns the narrative from action to verdict, pivoting away from the just-completed Baal purge to weigh Jehu against the calves of Bethel and Dan; this is a real edge but a softer one than the formulas bracketing the other rows in this part, since רַק opens no dated accession and no messenger dispatch. One member of the evaluation does carry a genuine opener candidate of its own -- 10:32's fronted temporal frame בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם (oshb:2Kgs.10.32) recurs byte-identical at 15:37 and 20:1, opening fresh episodes at both later occurrences -- but here it is held inside the evaluation because no closing or source-citation formula intervenes between it and 10:34-36, which closes the whole reign at once; 10:30's divine address to Jehu, by contrast, is unmediated first-person speech (וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל יֵה֗וּא) rather than a commissioned-messenger dispatch, so it does not belong to the same opener class as בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם and is content internal to the verdict, not a competing seam. The samekh after 10:29 (oshb, single-witness) marks this same soft internal turn without lifting it into a boundary, and the unit closes on the reign-length notice, וְהַיָּמִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר מָלַ֤ךְ יֵהוּא֙ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וּשְׁמֹנֶֽה שָׁנָ֖ה בְּשֹׁמְרֽוֹן (oshb:2Kgs.10.36) -- in fact a book-unique postponed reign-length notice standing after the burial-and-succession formula at 10:35, a construction found nowhere else in 2Kgs against the ordinary practice of folding reign length into the accession synchronism (13:1, 13:10) -- with a petuchah following in the WLC (oshb, single-witness) at the part's final verse.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The genuinely strongest rival splits at 10:32's בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם, since that same fronted frame opens fresh episodes elsewhere in the book (15:37, 20:1); it is set aside here only because no closing formula falls between the evaluation and the territorial notice, so 10:29-33 stays annalistically bound together until 10:34-36 closes the whole reign at once.

boundary_rationale: The row opens the part on Athaliah's own perception triggering her initiative: the verse's actual head is the disjunctive וַֽעֲתַלְיָה֙ אֵ֣ם אֲחַזְיָ֔הוּ וראתה רָאֲתָ֖ה כִּ֣י מֵ֣ת בְּנָ֑הּ (oshb:2Kgs.11.1) -- the ketiv/qere pair sits on the verb 'she saw' (וראתה / רָאֲתָ֖ה), not on the opening name -- before the wayyiqtol pair וַתָּ֨קָם֙ וַתְּאַבֵּ֔ד אֵ֖ת כָּל זֶ֥רַע הַמַּמְלָכָֽה (oshb:2Kgs.11.1) carries out the massacre itself; no antecedent formula demands a seam before this verse. It runs through Jehosheba's rescue (11:2) to a durative closing clause, וַיְהִ֤י אִתָּהּ֙ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה מִתְחַבֵּ֖א שֵׁ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֑ים וַעֲתַלְיָ֖ה מֹלֶ֥כֶת עַל הָאָֽרֶץ (oshb:2Kgs.11.3), whose six-year summary state stands apart from the punctual, dated opener of 11:4, וּבַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַ֠שְּׁבִיעִית שָׁלַ֨ח יְהוֹיָדָ֜ע (oshb:2Kgs.11.4). The pe mark after 11:3 (oshb:2Kgs.11.3, single-witness) gives weak corroboration for this edge but is not itself the reason for it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The strongest rival folds 11:1-3 into one undivided arc extending through 11:20, but the shift from the hidden child's durative six-year state to Jehoiada's freshly dated initiative marks a genuine pivot, not mere continuation.

boundary_rationale: Jehoiada's initiative opens on the dated formula וּבַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַ֠שְּׁבִיעִית שָׁלַ֨ח יְהוֹיָדָ֜ע ... וַיִּכְרֹת֩ לָהֶ֨ם בְּרִ֜ית (oshb:2Kgs.11.4), and the guard-mustering, coronation, execution, covenant, and Baal-purge that follow form one continuous coup-day scene. Samekh marks stand at 11:12, 11:14, and 11:16 (oshb, single-witness), punctuating internal turns within that same scene; the sharpest candidate among them falls at 11:16/11:17, where Jehoiada's second covenant opens וַיִּכְרֹ֨ת יְהוֹיָדָ֜ע אֶֽת הַבְּרִ֗ית (oshb:2Kgs.11.17) and 11:18 shifts subject and site to the Baal-temple crowd, but testing that seam only reinforces the unity claim: וַיִּכְרֹ֨ת at 11:17 answers וַיִּכְרֹת֩ לָהֶ֨ם בְּרִ֜ית at 11:4 in a covenant inclusio framing the entire coup day, not a fresh opening. It closes on the rest formula and its resumptive tail together: וַיִּשְׂמַ֥ח כָּל עַם הָאָ֖רֶץ וְהָעִ֣יר שָׁקָ֑טָה, continuing to the recapitulated execution clause that ends the verse, וְאֶת עֲתַלְיָ֛הוּ הֵמִ֥יתוּ בַחֶ֖רֶב בֵּ֥ית מלך הַמֶּֽלֶךְ (oshb:2Kgs.11.20, the closing ketiv/qere pair מלך / הַמֶּֽלֶךְ), which recaps the execution already narrated at וַתּוּמַ֖ת שָֽׁם (11:16); the samekh after 11:20 (oshb, single-witness) sits at this row's full outer edge, immediately before the age-formula opens fresh at web:2Kgs.11.21 = oshb:2Kgs.12.1 (MT), Jehoash's accession notice.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The genuinely strongest rival splits at 11:16/11:17, where Jehoiada's covenant-making and the crowd's move to Baal's temple could be read as a fresh initiative following the execution just narrated; but וַיִּכְרֹ֨ת יְהוֹיָדָ֜ע אֶֽת הַבְּרִ֗ית at 11:17 deliberately answers the covenant already cut at 11:4, forming an inclusio that binds the whole coup day into one scene rather than opening a second one.

boundary_rationale: Both edges of this row sit inside the book's sole numbering fork, so each Hebrew form below is cross-referenced to its MT slot one verse higher than its WEB number. The row opens on the age-clause בֶּן שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִ֖ים יְהוֹאָ֥שׁ בְּמָלְכֽוֹ (web:2Kgs.11.21 = oshb:2Kgs.12.1, MT), continues through the accession synchronism and reign length (web:2Kgs.12.1 = oshb:2Kgs.12.2, MT), the evaluation וַיַּ֨עַשׂ יְהוֹאָ֧שׁ הַיָּשָׁ֛ר בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה כָּל יָמָ֑יו אֲשֶׁ֣ר הוֹרָ֔הוּ יְהוֹיָדָ֖ע הַכֹּהֵֽן (web:2Kgs.12.2 = oshb:2Kgs.12.3, MT), and the high-places caveat רַ֥ק הַבָּמ֖וֹת לֹא סָ֑רוּ (web:2Kgs.12.3 = oshb:2Kgs.12.4, MT). It closes there because the next verse pivots to direct royal speech on a new topic, וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוֹאָ֜שׁ אֶל הַכֹּהֲנִ֗ים (web:2Kgs.12.4 = oshb:2Kgs.12.5, MT), opening the repair mandate. A pe stands at MT 12:1 = WEB 11:21 (oshb, single-witness), exactly where a one-verse split would cut, but as weak corroboration it favors that rejected reading rather than driving it, and the tier-1 ground for keeping the age-clause bound to the synchronism, evaluation, and caveat that follow -- the synchronism at MT 12:2 completes the same Jehoash accession begun by the age-clause at MT 12:1; no second king's accession opens there -- remains the actual reason the row holds together at high confidence.
strongest_rejected_alternative: One could isolate 11:21 as its own one-verse row -- a reading the single-witness pe at MT 12:1 (= WEB 11:21) weakly corroborates -- but the age-clause and the synchronism, evaluation, and caveat verses that follow it form a single accession unit on tier-1 grounds, since no accession formula restarts at MT 12:2.

boundary_rationale: Because this whole span falls in the WEB/MT offset stretch, every Hebrew citation below trails its MT verse number, one higher than the WEB count. Jehoash's mandate opens the account (web:2Kgs.12.4 = oshb:2Kgs.12.5, MT); the account then absorbs its own failure and remedy -- לֹֽא חִזְּק֥וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים אֶת בֶּ֥דֶק הַבָּֽיִת at the twenty-third-year date formula (web:2Kgs.12.6 = oshb:2Kgs.12.7, MT) -- as one plotted whole rather than two, since the chest-procedure that follows is presented as the direct fix for the failure just reported, not as a new topic. It closes on the fiscal exemption כֶּ֤סֶף אָשָׁם֙ וְכֶ֣סֶף חַטָּא֔וֹת לֹ֥א יוּבָ֖א בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה לַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים יִהְיֽוּ (web:2Kgs.12.16 = oshb:2Kgs.12.17, MT), a caveat clause paralleling the high-places caveat that closed the previous row, before אָ֣ז יַעֲלֶ֗ה חֲזָאֵל֙ (web:2Kgs.12.17 = oshb:2Kgs.12.18, MT) pivots to an external campaign. This is the part's flagged low-confidence pivot, and both single-witness marks belong on the record: a pe falls at MT 12:6 (= web:2Kgs.12.5), landing exactly where an alternate two-row reading would draw its seam, while a second pe falls at this row's own closing edge, MT 12:17 (= web:2Kgs.12.16, oshb, single-witness), corroborating the accepted close rather than only the rejected split.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The best rival segmentation splits at the twenty-third-year failure notice (12:4-5 mandate versus 12:6-16 remedy), a reading the single-witness pe at that very point would support, but it is set aside because the mandate-failure-remedy sequence reads as one continuous procedural plot rather than two independently opened units.

boundary_rationale: This short span still sits inside the offset run, so its citations carry their MT equivalents, one verse ahead of WEB, alongside the WEB reference. The adverb אָ֣ז ('then') in אָ֣ז יַעֲלֶ֗ה חֲזָאֵל֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָ֔ם וַיִּלָּ֥חֶם עַל גַּ֖ת וַֽיִּלְכְּדָ֑הּ (web:2Kgs.12.17 = oshb:2Kgs.12.18, MT) pivots the narrative into a fresh event chain rather than continuing the repair account, and the scene resolves within these two verses when Jehoash strips the treasuries and Hazael וַיַּ֖עַל מֵעַ֥ל יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם, went away from Jerusalem (web:2Kgs.12.18 = oshb:2Kgs.12.19, MT). The next verse reopens with the source-citation formula וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י יוֹאָ֖שׁ (web:2Kgs.12.19 = oshb:2Kgs.12.20, MT), a hallmark regnal-closing opener distinct in kind from this campaign notice.
strongest_rejected_alternative: One might fold this campaign notice into the following conspiracy-close row as a single external-threat-plus-reign-end unit, but the source-citation formula that opens 12:19 is this book's standing closing-unit marker and stands on its own regardless of what precedes it.

boundary_rationale: Sitting at the tail of the offset run, this row still needs its citations paired one final time before WEB and MT converge at chapter 13. The unit opens on the closing citation וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י יוֹאָ֖שׁ וְכָל אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲלוֹא הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה (web:2Kgs.12.19 = oshb:2Kgs.12.20, MT), then swaps in the assassination formula וַיָּקֻ֥מוּ עֲבָדָ֖יו וַיִּקְשְׁרֽוּ קָ֑שֶׁר (web:2Kgs.12.20 = oshb:2Kgs.12.21, MT) where a peaceful death notice would ordinarily stand. The killers surface by name at web:2Kgs.12.21 = oshb:2Kgs.12.22 (MT), and the witnesses part company there: WEB gives 'Jozacar the son of Shimeath' for the first assassin while MT reads וְיוֹזָבָ֣ד בֶּן שִׁ֠מְעָת, a genuine name variant kept visible rather than harmonized away. Amaziah's succession closes the unit in the same verse, and the fresh synchronism at 2Kgs.13.1 opens the next reign outside the offset zone entirely.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A minority reading folds the source-citation formula into the preceding tribute notice as one long close, but that formula still opens this row's near edge on its own; what needs correcting is only the claim that it marks every reign's end in this framework — a book-wide count finds it at 22 verses while seven reigns, including Joram of Israel, Athaliah, and Hoshea, receive no such citation at all, so the formula is better described as this framework's recurring, not universal, closing marker.
boundary_evidence_refs: web:2Kgs.12.21 = oshb:2Kgs.12.22 (MT, name variant: WEB Jozacar / MT ויוזבד)

boundary_rationale: Numbering has fully realigned by this point, so citations run single from here to the part's end. Jehoahaz's frame opens on the synchronistic formula בִּשְׁנַ֨ת עֶשְׂרִ֤ים וְשָׁלֹשׁ֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לְיוֹאָ֥שׁ ... מָ֠לַךְ יְהוֹאָחָ֨ז (oshb:2Kgs.13.1) and proceeds through a brief evaluation into the deliverance episode. That episode's wayyiqtol chain is confined to 13:4-5, וַיְחַ֥ל יְהוֹאָחָ֖ז אֶת פְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה and וַיִּתֵּ֨ן יְהוָ֤ה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מוֹשִׁ֔יעַ, while 13:6-7 shift register to a narrator's aside: 13:6 opens אַ֠ךְ לֹֽא סָ֜רוּ מֵחַטֹּ֧אות בֵּית יָרָבְעָ֛ם, a restrictive-particle-plus-qatal construction, and closes on the disjunctive וְגַם֙ הָאֲשֵׁרָ֔ה עָמְדָ֖ה בְּשֹׁמְרֽוֹן, while 13:7 continues on causal כִּ֣י לֹא֩ הִשְׁאִ֨יר. None of these interior clauses opens a fresh unit; the WEB editorial parenthesis brackets only 13:5-6, per 2Kgs_web_clean.txt, and is noted here as layout, not a boundary signal. The frame closes on the paired formulas וְיֶ֨תֶר דִּבְרֵ֧י יְהוֹאָחָ֛ז ... הֲלוֹא הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים (13:8) and וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב יְהֽוֹאָחָז֙ עִם אֲבֹתָ֔יו ... וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יוֹאָ֥שׁ בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו (oshb:2Kgs.13.9), with the pe trailing 13:9 offering only weak, single-witness support behind the closing pair. Jehoash's own synchronism opens fresh at 13:10.
strongest_rejected_alternative: One could still carve out 13:4-7 as its own row, but 13:4-5's wayyiqtol chain continues the Jehoahaz narrative rather than opening anything, and 13:6-7 read as the narrator's own evaluative and causal asides rather than a formula-marked insertion, so the whole deliverance passage stays inside the reign unit it serves.

boundary_rationale: Jehoash of Israel's reign opens on its own synchronism, בִּשְׁנַ֨ת שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וָשֶׁ֨בַע֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לְיוֹאָ֖שׁ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה מָ֠לַךְ יְהוֹאָ֨שׁ בֶּן יְהוֹאָחָ֤ז (oshb:2Kgs.13.10), followed by a brief evaluation (13:11) and the paired closing formulas, וְיֶ֨תֶר דִּבְרֵ֤י יוֹאָשׁ֙ ... אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִלְחַ֔ם עִ֖ם אֲמַצְיָ֣ה (13:12) and וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב יוֹאָשׁ֙ עִם אֲבֹתָ֔יו וְיָרָבְעָ֖ם יָשַׁ֣ב עַל כִּסְא֑וֹ (oshb:2Kgs.13.13), corroborated only weakly by the trailing pe (single-witness). The next verse pivots genre rather than cast: וֶֽאֱלִישָׁע֙ חָלָ֣ה אֶת חָלְי֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָמ֖וּת בּ֑וֹ (13:14) opens on a fronted, disjunctive subject before the narrative resumes with וַיֵּ֨רֶד אֵלָ֜יו יוֹאָ֣שׁ מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל — the very king whose reign report just closed re-enters at once as mourner, so it is the shift from regnal-framework register to prophetic sign-act narrative that grounds the split, not any exit of Jehoash from the stage.
strongest_rejected_alternative: One might keep this reign notice bundled with what follows on the strength of the shared king, but that argument only works if 13:14 removed Jehoash from the account entirely; instead he re-enters at once as the weeping visitor, so the seam has to rest on the switch from closing formula to disjunctive narrative opening, a distinction that holds regardless of his continued presence.

boundary_rationale: This remains the part's other flagged low-confidence stretch, so its row count is argued rather than assumed. The unit opens on the illness notice and royal lament, וֶֽאֱלִישָׁע֙ חָלָ֣ה אֶת חָלְי֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָמ֖וּת בּ֑וֹ ... אָבִ֣י אָבִ֔י רֶ֥כֶב יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וּפָרָשָֽׁיו (oshb:2Kgs.13.14) — the same cry, consonantally identical though differently accented, אָבִ֣י אָבִ֗י רֶ֤כֶב יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וּפָ֣רָשָׁ֔יו, that Elisha spoke over Elijah's ascent (oshb:2Kgs.2.12), a phrase exclusive to these two verses book-wide and one that frames Elisha's own death as a matched career bracket rather than mere continuation. It runs through the bow-and-arrow rite to the rebuke-oracle אָ֛ז הִכִּ֥יתָ אֶת אֲרָ֖ם עַד כַּלֵּ֑ה וְעַתָּ֕ה שָׁלֹ֥שׁ פְּעָמִ֖ים תַּכֶּ֥ה אֶת אֲרָֽם (oshb:2Kgs.13.19), a self-contained closural speech-act with the samekh trailing it offering the same weak corroboration seen elsewhere. What follows at 13:20 does not stage new, unnamed figures at the seam itself: its first clause, וַיָּ֥מָת אֱלִישָׁ֖ע וַֽיִּקְבְּרֻ֑הוּ, resolves the death this very row announced at 13:14, naming Elisha rather than an anonymous man, while its second clause, וּגְדוּדֵ֥י מוֹאָ֛ב יָבֹ֥אוּ בָאָ֖רֶץ בָּ֥א שָׁנָֽה, brings on the Moabite raiders that the following row's vignette develops; the unnamed corpse thrown into Elisha's tomb belongs to 13:21, a full verse later. The row still ends at 13:19 because the rebuke-oracle is a complete closural speech-act and verse-tiling forbids splitting 13:20 to reach it, not because 13:20 stages a different cast.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The competing view merges this with the bones vignette as one longer Elisha-death complex, but 13:19's rebuke-oracle already closes as a self-contained speech-act, and the tiling rule keeps the row from reaching into 13:20 to grab a scene change that in any case only partly materializes there — the actual change of cast waits for 13:21, which the following row carries.

boundary_rationale: Verse 20 does double duty: its first clause, וַיָּ֥מָת אֱלִישָׁ֖ע וַֽיִּקְבְּרֻ֑הוּ, closes the illness notice opened at 13:14, while its second, וּגְדוּדֵ֥י מוֹאָ֛ב יָבֹ֥אוּ בָאָ֖רֶץ בָּ֥א שָׁנָֽה (oshb:2Kgs.13.20), stages the raiders this vignette needs; because rows tile at verse edges, the whole verse sits here with the story its second half launches. The near edge is not argued from that clause in isolation: 13:21 opens וַיְהִ֞י הֵ֣ם קֹבְרִ֣ים אִ֗ישׁ וְהִנֵּה֙ רָא֣וּ אֶֽת הַגְּד֔וּד, a wayehi-plus-participle frame with a וְהִנֵּה֙ apodosis that is itself a recognized scene-opening construction, but its definite article on הַגְּד֔וּד already presupposes an antecedent (the noun itself shifts number here, from a plural construct to this singular definite), and that antecedent is most readily supplied by the וּגְדוּדֵ֥י מוֹאָ֛ב just named in 13:20b — so the raider clause, not the burial notice, is what actually opens the vignette. The unit closes at וַיִּגַּ֤ע הָאִישׁ֙ בְּעַצְמ֣וֹת אֱלִישָׁ֔ע וַיְחִ֖י וַיָּ֥קָם עַל רַגְלָֽיו (oshb:2Kgs.13.21), with the trailing pe (single-witness) offering further, still-weak confirmation before 13:22 returns to the political register with an entirely different subject.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A cleaner-looking split would keep 13:14-20 together as the full death notice and start the bones story only at 13:21 — a genuine rival, since it cuts cleanly at a verse edge rather than mid-clause — but 13:21's own definite הַגְּד֔וּד needs the antecedent 13:20b already supplies, so the vignette's real opening clause has to be the raider notice, not the burial verb.

boundary_rationale: The row opens on a retrospective political summary unlike the tomb miracle just told, וַֽחֲזָאֵל֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָ֔ם לָחַ֖ץ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י יְהוֹאָחָֽז (oshb:2Kgs.13.22), grounds Israel's reprieve in covenant memory at 13:23, and reports Hazael's death and succession at 13:24 before closing on an explicit fulfillment: שָׁלֹ֤שׁ פְּעָמִים֙ הִכָּ֣הוּ יוֹאָ֔שׁ וַיָּ֖שֶׁב אֶת עָרֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:2Kgs.13.25) echoes the שָׁלֹ֥שׁ פְּעָמִ֖ים תַּכֶּ֥ה אֶת אֲרָֽם count set by the sign-act oracle at oshb:2Kgs.13.19. A trailing pe (single-witness) sits at this row's own edge, but the edge is actually carried by the next unit's tier-1 opener rather than by that mark: 2Kgs.14.1 opens on the fresh accession synchronism בִּשְׁנַ֣ת שְׁתַּ֔יִם לְיוֹאָ֥שׁ בֶּן יוֹאָחָ֖ז מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מָלַ֛ךְ אֲמַצְיָ֥הוּ בֶן יוֹאָ֖שׁ, one of fifteen verse-initial בשנת year-formula clauses, fourteen of them accession openers counted across the book (17:6's בִּשְׁנַ֨ת הַתְּשִׁיעִ֜ית לְהוֹשֵׁ֗עַ לָכַ֤ד מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר֙ instead dates the king of Assyria's capture of Samaria, not a new king's accession), so the far edge rests on that formula, leaving the mark as secondary, single-witness support alone.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The alternative treats 13:20-25 as one six-verse aftermath row, but 13:22's pivot to Hazael's decades-long oppression and Yahweh's covenant compassion has no link to the anonymous-corpse miracle beyond bare sequence, and the topic change is confirmed independently by 14:1's own accession formula opening a wholly new reign report, so the earlier miracle keeps its own row.

literature_type_guess: regnal_framework_notice (Amaziah of Judah, opening formula and Edom-conquest notice)
boundary_rationale: The row opens on the double accession-and-evaluation formula בִּשְׁנַ֣ת שְׁתַּ֔יִם לְיוֹאָ֥שׁ...מָלַ֛ךְ אֲמַצְיָ֥הוּ בֶן יוֹאָ֖שׁ (14:1), continued through the age notice and the evaluation verdict הַיָּשָׁר֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה (14:3), which this Judahite run's other reigns echo in their own terms — 15:3's וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הַיָּשָׁ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂ֖ה אֲמַצְיָ֥הוּ אָבִֽיו and 15:34's וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הַיָּשָׁ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כְּכֹ֧ל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂ֛ה עֻזִיָּ֥הוּ אָבִ֖יו. The רַ֕ק לֹ֖א כְּדָוִ֣ד אָבִ֑יו qualifier that follows in 14:3 belongs to Amaziah specifically: a book-wide search finds כדוד only here and, negated, at כְּדָוִ֥ד אָבִֽיו (16:2), while Jehoash's own notice measures him against Jehoiada instead, אֲשֶׁ֣ר הוֹרָ֔הוּ יְהוֹיָדָ֖ע הַכֹּהֵֽן (12:3). Its far edge is the etiological tag עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה sealing the Sela/Edom victory notice at 14:7, weakly seconded by a single-witness pe at the same verse. The messenger clause that follows, אָ֣ז שָׁלַ֤ח אֲמַצְיָה֙ מַלְאָכִ֔ים (14:8), does not introduce a new participant — 14:7 has already fronted Amaziah as הוּא הִכָּ֨ה אֶת אֱד֤וֹם — but it does open a fresh scene: its אָז governs a qatal verb, שָׁלַ֤ח, unlike the yiqtol forms governed by the book's other verse-initial אָז clauses at 12:18, 15:16, and 16:5, marking 14:8 as a distinct construction rather than mere continuation of the annalistic notice. The amnesty-law citation at 14:6 stays interior, elaborating the killed-servants notice of 14:5 rather than opening anything of its own.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding 14:7's Edom victory into the following Beth-shemesh unit as its provocation is the nearest competitor, but 14:8's messenger clause turns on a marked אָז-plus-qatal construction found at no other verse-initial אָז in this book, and that grammatical distinctiveness, not a change of participant, is what keeps the annalistic 'he struck' notice and the embassy scene apart.

boundary_rationale: The unit's true clause-initial opener is אָ֣ז שָׁלַ֤ח אֲמַצְיָה֙ מַלְאָכִ֔ים (14:8) — one of only four verse-initial אָז clauses in the book (12:18, 14:8, 15:16, 16:5) and the sole one governing a suffix-conjugation verb — with the embassy content, לְכָ֖ה נִתְרָאֶ֥ה פָנִֽים, following לֵאמֹ֑ר as its thematic signature rather than its grammatical marker. Jehoash answers with the thistle-and-cedar fable הַח֜וֹחַ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּלְּבָנ֗וֹן (14:9), and the challenge resolves when the narrative echoes the same verb as accomplishment, וַיִּתְרָא֣וּ פָנִ֔ים (14:11), at Beth-shemesh. Rather than break at the plunder of Jerusalem (14:14), the row extends through the source-citation and death-burial-succession triad of 14:15-16, וְיֶתֶר֩ דִּבְרֵ֨י יְהוֹאָ֜שׁ...וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יָרָבְעָ֥ם בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו; this is a variant doublet of Jehoash's earlier closing formula rather than a plain repeat — 13:12 keeps וְכָל אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה where 14:15 drops it, and 13:13 places יָרָבְעָ֖ם יָשַׁ֣ב עַל כִּסְא֑וֹ before the burial verb where 14:16 places וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יָרָבְעָ֥ם בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו after it — so it reads as this clash narrative's own resumptive close for the victor rather than a detached, duplicated notice; the pe recorded at MT 14:16 lends only weak, single-witness backing to that outer edge.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Setting 14:15-16 apart as its own row remains arguable given the doublet with 13:12-13, but a source-citation formula never opens a unit by itself, and nothing at 14:15 marks a fresh scene, so this stays the clash narrative's trailing close — hence medium rather than high confidence.

literature_type_guess: regnal_framework_notice (Amaziah of Judah, closing formula, conspiracy, and Azariah succession)
boundary_rationale: This row resumes where the foreign king's death notice ends, marked by the distinctive 'lived after' formula וַיְחִ֨י אֲמַצְיָ֤הוּ בֶן יוֹאָשׁ֙...אַֽחֲרֵ֣י מ֔וֹת יְהוֹאָ֥שׁ (14:17) rather than the ordinary accession pattern, followed by Amaziah's own source citation (14:18) and the cognate-accusative conspiracy notice וַיִּקְשְׁר֨וּ עָלָ֥יו קֶ֛שֶׁר בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם (14:19), where the finite verb and its object noun share the same root. The one genuinely marked construction in this span sits at its own tail rather than at 14:21, which opens on the plain wayyiqtol וַיִּקְח֞וּ with no signal of a break, though the same verse's own fronted pronoun, וְה֕וּא בֶּן שֵׁ֥שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָ֑ה, heads a subordinate circumstantial clause mid-verse rather than marking a break itself, which if anything strengthens rather than weakens the case for keeping 14:21 interior: 14:22 fronts an independent pronoun before a suffix-conjugation verb, ה֚וּא בָּנָ֣ה אֶת אֵילַ֔ת, one of only six verse-initial הוּא clauses in the whole book (14:7, 14:22, 14:25, 15:12, 18:4, 18:8). That construction stays bound to this row because its own tail, אַחֲרֵ֥י שְׁכַֽב הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ עִם אֲבֹתָֽיו, anchors the Elath notice backward to Amaziah's death just narrated, functioning as a summarizing appendix rather than a fresh opening; MT's pe after 14:22 offers weak, single-witness corroboration for that reading, before the next verse's Israelite accession synchronism opens Jeroboam's own frame.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the conspiracy notice from the Azariah/Elath succession at 14:21 looks tempting given the wayyiqtol there, but that verb form marks no discontinuity at all; the passage's real candidate seam is 14:22's fronted הוּא construction, and even that stays interior once its own back-reference to Amaziah's death is weighed, so the row keeps its full extent.

literature_type_guess: regnal_framework_notice (Jeroboam II of Israel, with Jonah fulfillment notice)
boundary_rationale: The Israelite accession synchronism בִּשְׁנַת֙ חֲמֵשׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה לַאֲמַצְיָ֥הוּ...מָ֠לַךְ יָרָבְעָ֨ם (14:23) opens Jeroboam II's reign, and the unit runs to the standard source-citation and death-succession close at 14:28-29, with a single-witness pe at 14:29 offering weak corroboration only. Inside the frame, the territorial-restoration notice at 14:25 does not open on its fulfillment tag; its governing clause is the independent, fronted-pronoun construction ה֗וּא הֵשִׁיב֙ אֶת גְּב֣וּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל, with the anchor כִּדְבַ֤ר יְהוָה֙...אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֗ר בְּיַד עַבְדּ֞וֹ יוֹנָ֤ה בֶן אֲמִתַּי֙ הַנָּבִ֔יא subordinate to it. That same fronted-הוּא device recurs at 14:7 and 14:22 in this same run, and in each case functions as a summarizing notice bound to the reign report it sits in rather than as an accession-style opening, so 14:25 stays interior on those grounds rather than because it lacks an opening formula of its own -- before 15:1's own accession synchronism opens the next unit.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating the Jonah fulfillment notice as its own row would isolate what is, in fact, an independent fronted-pronoun clause rather than a bare dependent one, but the same construction recurring at 14:7 and 14:22 consistently marks a summarizing aside inside a reign report, not a fresh unit, so 14:25 stays bound to Jeroboam's frame.

literature_type_guess: regnal_framework_notice (Azariah/Uzziah of Judah, with leprosy and co-regency notice)
boundary_rationale: Azariah's reign opens on the standard synchronism בִּשְׁנַ֨ת עֶשְׂרִ֤ים וָשֶׁ֨בַע֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לְיָרָבְעָ֖ם...מָלַ֛ךְ עֲזַרְיָ֥ה (15:1) and closes on the death-burial-succession triad (15:7); weak, single-witness corroboration appears in the pe following MT 15:7. Uniquely for this reign, the frame carries its own medical notice, וַיְנַגַּ֨ע יְהוָ֜ה אֶת הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ וַיְהִ֤י מְצֹרָע֙ (15:5), plus a co-regency clause naming Jotham as judging the people of the land, both staying interior rather than triggering a seam of their own.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The leprosy notice and Jotham co-regency (15:5) could be read as opening a distinct administrative unit, but neither carries an accession-year formula, so both remain inside Azariah's single reign report.

literature_type_guess: regnal_framework_notice (Zechariah of Israel, with Jehu-dynasty fulfillment aside)
boundary_rationale: Zechariah's six-month reign opens with בִּשְׁנַ֨ת שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וּשְׁמֹנֶה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לַעֲזַרְיָ֖הוּ...זְכַרְיָ֨הוּ (15:8) and is struck down within the same short unit by Shallum's conspiracy, וַיִּקְשֹׁ֤ר עָלָיו֙ שַׁלֻּ֣ם בֶּן יָבֵ֔שׁ (15:10). The source-citation formula that would ordinarily close the report has already run its course at 15:11, וְיֶ֖תֶר דִּבְרֵ֣י זְכַרְיָ֑ה הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים; the fulfillment aside that follows opens on its own disjunctive construction, ה֣וּא דְבַר יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֤ר אֶל יֵהוּא֙, a verbless clause with a fronted pronoun standing apart from what precedes rather than completing it, and resolves the four-generation promise with וַֽיְהִי כֵֽן (15:12). Read this way the aside terminates Zechariah's frame as a narrator's appended comment rather than as a grammatical continuation of an already-closed citation; the pe after MT 15:12 supplies weak, single-witness corroboration alone before 15:13 opens on its subject-first accession formula, שַׁלּ֤וּם בֶּן יָבֵישׁ֙ מָלַ֔ךְ, with the synchronism following rather than leading.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 15:12 as belonging with Shallum's following reign is the chief competitor, since Shallum's own act fulfills the promise, but the disjunctive fronted-pronoun clause that opens it stands apart from 15:13's fresh synchronism just as much as from 15:11's finished citation, and as an appended comment it reads more naturally as sealing the frame just closed than as launching the next one.
