The unit closes on כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֔ר בְּיַ֖ד כָּל עֲבָדָ֣יו הַנְּבִיאִ֑ים...עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה (17:23), a boundary the pe mark after MT 17:23 corroborates weakly.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The strongest competing cut isolates 17:18-20 as a Judah-notice-and-Jeroboam-retrospect digression, but 17:23 does not introduce the removal verb for the first time -- it resumes the identical מֵעַ֣ל פָּנָ֑יו idiom 17:18 already supplied -- so the resumptive echo binds rather than divides the intervening material, defeating the split on stronger grounds than a merely delayed verb.

boundary_rationale: A fresh subject sets this narrative in motion: וַיָּבֵ֣א מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁ֡וּר מִבָּבֶ֡ל וּ֠מִכּוּ֠תָה וּמֵעַוָּ֤א וּמֵֽחֲמָת֙ וּסְפַרְוַ֔יִם (17:24), replacing the deported Israelites with imported settlers right after the homily's close, and crisis follows at לֹ֥א יָרְא֖וּ אֶת יְהוָ֑ה (17:25). The royal command of 17:27 resolves into וַֽיְהִי֙ מוֹרֶ֣ה אֹתָ֔ם אֵ֖יךְ יִֽירְא֥וּ אֶת יְהוָֽה (17:28), though the Hebrew itself does not mark a hard stop there: 17:29 opens on the identical wayyiqtol-of-hayah-plus-participle frame, וַיִּהְי֣וּ עֹשִׂ֔ים גּ֥וֹי גּ֖וֹי, a construction that already recurs inside this span at 17:25 (וַיִּֽהְי֥וּ הֹרְגִ֖ים בָּהֶֽם) and continues past the cut at 17:29, 17:32 (twice), and 17:41. What actually discriminates the seam is content rather than grammar -- one priest resolving a single lion crisis for the whole resettled population gives way to a plural, per-nation cult catalogue that reopens rather than sustains that resolution -- so the row's cut is honestly carried by narrative arc alone. No parashah mark falls inside this stretch either, leaving the seam argued purely on that content-level turn.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this account together with 17:29-33 into one undifferentiated resettlement report was weighed, and the shared periphrastic construction at 17:28/17:29 gives that reading real grammatical support, but the turn from one priest's resolved teaching to the nations' ongoing per-nation gods is a genuine content discriminator a single span would erase.

boundary_rationale: Where 17:28 left a settled outcome, 17:29 does not pivot on its own clause type -- its וַיִּהְי֣וּ עֹשִׂ֔ים גּ֥וֹי גּ֖וֹי אֱלֹהָ֑יו repeats the same periphrastic hayah-plus-participle construction that closed 17:28's וַֽיְהִי֙ מוֹרֶ֣ה אֹתָ֔ם and recurs again at 17:32's וַיִּהְי֛וּ עֹשִׂ֥ים לָהֶ֖ם, so no disjunctive marker actually falls at this precise seam. What opens the register is instead the distributive doubled noun גּ֥וֹי גּ֖וֹי אֱלֹהָ֑יו itself, already present in 17:29, and the waw-subject-qatal list clauses that build out the catalogue proper beginning at 17:30, וְאַנְשֵׁ֣י בָבֶ֗ל עָשׂוּ֙ / וְאַנְשֵׁי כ֔וּת עָשׂ֖וּ. The register lands on the fronted verdict אֶת יְהוָ֖ה הָי֣וּ יְרֵאִ֑ים וְאֶת אֱלֹֽהֵיהֶם֙ הָי֣וּ עֹֽבְדִ֔ים (17:33), stating the double-cult judgment the list was building toward. Neither edge carries a parashah mark, so this seam is argued from the distributive noun and the catalogue syntax rather than from any contrastive clause type at the 28/29 boundary itself.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this register through 17:40 as a single syncretism unit has some thematic pull, but 17:34 shifts abruptly into homiletic third-person narration (עַ֣ד הַיּ֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ הֵ֣ם עֹשִׂ֔ים ... אֵינָ֤ם יְרֵאִים֙ אֶת יְהוָ֔ה), and the quoted covenant stipulation itself only opens at 17:35 (וַיְצַוֵּ֣ם לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹ֥א תִֽירְא֖וּ אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים) -- a mode the peoples list never adopts, so merging the two spans would flatten a genuine change of voice.

boundary_rationale: The left edge is sharper than a shared idiom alone would suggest: 17:33's fronted verdict אֶת יְהוָ֖ה הָי֣וּ יְרֵאִ֑ים is flatly reversed by 17:34's אֵינָ֤ם יְרֵאִים֙ אֶת יְהוָ֔ה, a contradiction the Hebrew states as a fronted-object reversal of the same verb and object (אֶת יְהוָ֖ה הָי֣וּ יְרֵאִ֑ים / אֵינָ֤ם יְרֵאִים֙ אֶת יְהוָ֔ה); WEB's own gloss ('They feared Yahweh' / ‘They don’t fear Yahweh’) preserves the propositional contradiction, though not the Hebrew's fronting. The homily opens on עַ֣ד הַיּ֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ הֵ֣ם עֹשִׂ֔ים כַּמִּשְׁפָּטִ֖ים הָרִֽאשֹׁנִ֑ים (17:34) and inside that frame shifts into quoted covenant terms addressed in second person, לֹ֥א תִֽירְא֖וּ אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים (17:35), a register the third-person peoples list just before it never adopts. The span's own close at 17:40, וְלֹ֖א שָׁמֵ֑עוּ כִּ֛י אִֽם כְּמִשְׁפָּטָ֥ם הָֽרִאשׁ֖וֹן הֵ֥ם עֹשִֽׂים, drops the second-person address entirely and is itself third-person plural throughout, so the covenant voice does not carry to the row's own edge; the closing idiom bracketing 34 and 40 also shifts from a plural-definite form (כַּמִּשְׁפָּטִ֖ים הָרִֽאשֹׁנִ֑ים) to a singular form with a third-person-plural suffix (כְּמִשְׁפָּטָ֥ם הָֽרִאשׁ֖וֹן), and both of its elements -- הֵ֣ם עֹשִׂ֔ים and עַ֣ד הַיּ֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ -- recur together again in 17:41's own closing clause, so what looked like a closed bracket is in fact a repetition that keeps running past this span's own edge. The internal covenant-address shift at 17:35 remains the row's genuine discriminator; the low-confidence flag governing this whole region still applies to how the span attaches to its neighbors.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 17:41 into this span to make one homily-plus-coda unit was considered, since both invoke 'to this day,' but the discriminator cannot be a person-register contrast, since 17:40 is already third-person throughout; the better ground for a separate closing row is 17:41's reintroduced definite-plural 'these nations' subject and its added three-generation clause, absent from 34-40.

boundary_rationale: This single verse closes the entire resettlement complex, not just the covenant homily beside it. Its subject, וַיִּהְי֣וּ הַגּוֹיִ֣ם הָאֵ֗לֶּה יְרֵאִים֙ אֶת יְהוָ֔ה (17:41), is a definite plural that echoes הַגּוֹיִ֗ם at 17:26 and הַגּוֹיִ֔ם at 17:33's closing formula rather than 17:29's distributive singular גּ֥וֹי גּ֖וֹי, so the discriminator is a reintroduced antecedent, not a person-register shift: 17:40, the verse this coda separates from, is itself already third-person plural throughout (שָׁמֵ֑עוּ, הֵ֥ם עֹשִֽׂים), so no second-to-third-person change occurs at this exact edge. What is new is the generational scope -- גַּם בְּנֵיהֶ֣ם וּבְנֵ֣י בְנֵיהֶ֗ם (17:41) states a three-generation continuity absent from every earlier verse in the chapter and, on a book-wide check, from the rest of 2Kgs as well. The pe mark set after MT 17:41 (petuchah, single-witness) flags this as the chapter's last macro-edge, joining the marks at 17:6 and 17:23 that likewise sit at this part's major seams, though as with every such mark it corroborates rather than drives the cut.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 17:41 as the closing verse of 34-40 rather than an independent coda stays defensible given the shared 'to this day' idiom, but since no person-register shift actually separates the two, the case for a fresh unit rests instead on the reintroduced definite-plural nations subject and the added sons'-sons clause -- a margin thin enough that this row is capped at medium_low.

boundary_rationale: The unit opens on the standard Judahite accession-synchronism formula וַֽיְהִי֙ בִּשְׁנַ֣ת שָׁלֹ֔שׁ לְהוֹשֵׁ֥עַ בֶּן אֵלָ֖ה מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מָלַ֛ךְ חִזְקִיָּ֥ה בֶן אָחָ֖ז מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה (18:1), pairing Hezekiah's reign start against Hoshea's regnal year the way the framework does throughout the dual-monarchy stretch. Rather than one unbroken subject chain -- 18:7 briefly hands the clause subject to Yahweh, וְהָיָ֤ה יְהוָה֙ עִמּ֔וֹ, before וַיִּמְרֹ֥ד בְּמֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁ֖וּר returns it to Hezekiah -- the span is held together by a matched fronted-pronoun pair: ה֣וּא הֵסִ֣יר אֶת הַבָּמ֗וֹת opens the reform notice at 18:4 and הֽוּא הִכָּ֧ה אֶת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֛ים עַד עַזָּ֖ה closes it at 18:8, the identical independent-pronoun-plus-qatal construction bracketing the reign summary from within rather than marking either verse as a break. A petuchah follows at MT 18:8, weakly corroborating the seam before the re-dated and doubled synchronism opening 18:9.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Peeling 18:4-8 off as a separate reform-acts unit fails because 18:4 opens with the same הוּא-fronted construction that recurs verse-initially at 18:8, the span's own closing verse, which reads as an internal frame rather than a fresh unit's opening formula.

boundary_rationale: A fresh double date formula launches this notice, וַֽיְהִ֞י בַּשָּׁנָ֤ה הָֽרְבִיעִית֙ לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ הִ֚יא הַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔ית לְהוֹשֵׁ֥עַ בֶּן אֵלָ֖ה מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (18:9), resuming and re-dating the Samaria siege already told at 17:5-6 as a resumptive retrospect. The Hoshea synchronism itself, לְהוֹשֵׁ֥עַ בֶּן אֵלָ֖ה מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל, is not new here -- the identical string already closes the date clause of 18:1, before its separate accession element מָלַ֛ךְ חִזְקִיָּ֥ה בֶן אָחָ֖ז מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה -- so what marks this notice off from 18:1-8 is instead the doubling of the date frame (הִ֚יא הַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔ית) and the inversion of which king's regnal count anchors it, Hezekiah's fourth year now given first where 18:1 gave only Hoshea's. It closes at 18:12 on the covenant-breach clause עַ֣ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא שָׁמְע֗וּ בְּקוֹל֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֔ם, with a petuchah following before 18:13 reopens with a different date and a different Assyrian king. Whether this four-verse retrospect stands alone or attaches forward remains genuinely arguable, since the re-dating device, not an arrival or commission formula, is what actually separates it from what surrounds it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Absorbing 18:9-12 into the tribute notice as one long Assyrian-pressure unit loses because 18:13 reopens with an independent fourteenth-year synchronism and swaps the actor from Shalmaneser to Sennacherib entirely.

boundary_rationale: This notice is framed by its own regnal-year date formula, not an accession date -- that belongs to 18:1's synchronism -- but Hezekiah's fourteenth year, וּבְאַרְבַּע֩ עֶשְׂרֵ֨ה שָׁנָ֜ה לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֗ה עָלָ֞ה סַנְחֵרִ֤יב (18:13), with Sennacherib replacing Shalmaneser as the actor, now moving against Judah's fortified cities rather than Samaria. It runs through the silver-and-gold settlement and ends at 18:16's temple-door stripping, בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא קִצַּ֨ץ חִזְקִיָּ֜ה אֶת דַּלְת֨וֹת הֵיכַ֤ל יְהוָה֙, where a petuchah is recorded. What follows at 18:17 is a dispatch-and-arrival formula rather than a muster -- וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁ֡וּר אֶת תַּרְתָּ֥ן וְאֶת רַב סָרִ֣יס וְאֶת רַב שָׁקֵ֨ה sends three named envoys, with arrival only supplied by the following וַֽיַּעֲלוּ֙ וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם and no mustering verb anywhere in the verse -- keeping this tribute record formally distinct from the embassy scene it precedes; source-critical theories that lump 18:13-17 together are not evidence for a different seam here.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 18:13-17 as one continuous crisis narrative loses because 18:17 introduces entirely new participants -- תַּרְתָּ֥ן וְאֶת רַב סָרִ֣יס וְאֶת רַב שָׁקֵ֨ה -- arriving via their own dispatch-and-arrival formula, absent from the brief tribute settlement of 18:13-16.

boundary_rationale: An embassy-arrival formula, וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁ֡וּר אֶת תַּרְתָּ֥ן וְאֶת רַב סָרִ֣יס וְאֶת רַב שָׁקֵ֨ה מִן לָכִ֜ישׁ אֶל הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֛הוּ בְּחֵ֥יל כָּבֵ֖ד יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם (18:17), introduces new officers, a great army, and the Jerusalem location, opening one continuous audience scene at the wall. The scene holds through three Rabshakeh speeches and the king's silencing order, closing only when the officials return to report, אֶל חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ קְרוּעֵ֣י בְגָדִ֑ים וַיַּגִּ֣דוּ ל֔וֹ דִּבְרֵ֖י רַב שָׁקֵֽה (18:37), the very report that triggers Hezekiah's reaction in 19:1. No participant, location, or arrival verb changes across the language-switch request or the second public speech, so those turns stay internal rather than becoming seams.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting a new unit where the officials ask for Aramaic and Rabshakeh instead shouts in Hebrew fails because both moves stay inside one unbroken audience before the same wall-sitting crowd, with no fresh muster or arrival verb marking any scene change.

boundary_rationale: This scene is triggered directly by the report that closed the audience: וַיְהִ֗י כִּשְׁמֹ֨עַ֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ וַיִּקְרַ֖ע אֶת בְּגָדָ֑יו (19:1) picks up 'hearing' as its hinge and relocates the action from the wall to the temple and then to Isaiah. It gathers the tearing of clothes, the delegation's message, and Isaiah's reply into one exchange, ending on the oracle's promise וְהִפַּלְתִּ֥יו בַּחֶ֖רֶב בְּאַרְצֽוֹ (19:7). The next verse abandons this court stage entirely, pivoting back to Rabshakeh's own movements at a new location, which marks the true seam.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 19:1-8 as one continuous Rabshakeh sequence loses because 19:8 drops the temple/Isaiah stage altogether, resuming Rabshakeh's itinerary with a location shift to Libnah that nothing in 19:1-7 anticipates.

boundary_rationale: A resumptive return-formula reopens the narrative on Rabshakeh at a fresh location, וַיָּ֨שָׁב֙ רַב שָׁקֵ֔ה וַיִּמְצָא֙ אֶת מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר נִלְחָ֖ם עַל לִבְנָ֑ה (19:8), then pivots to the king of Assyria's second dispatch, וַיָּ֨שָׁב֙ וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח מַלְאָכִ֔ים אֶל חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ (19:9), a verse closed by its own לֵאמֹֽר, the device that actually subordinates 19:10's content to the messengers already sent rather than commissioning new ones. 19:10 does open with its own messenger-speech formula, כֹּ֣ה תֹאמְר֗וּן, matching 19:6's כֹּ֥ה תֹאמְר֖וּן, so a formula genuinely stands there; what never recurs between the two verses is a new sending verb, and the letter's direct speech runs unbroken to its closing rhetorical questions, אַיּ֤וֹ מֶֽלֶךְ חֲמָת֙... (19:13). A pe is keyed to MT 19:14, one verse past this row's own close; per the marks-follow-their-verse convention it divides after 19:14 and, read alone, would group that verse backward with this embassy rather than corroborate the 19:13|19:14 seam the row closes on, so it is disclosed and set aside here as single-witness and non-driving, exactly as row M8-2Kgs-066 treats the same mark from the far side.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Stopping this row at 19:9 and treating 19:10-13 as an independently commissioned letter-content unit fails because no new sending or arrival verb intervenes at 19:10, whose content is subordinated by 19:9's own closing לֵאמֹֽר.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:2Kgs.19.14 (petuchah, single-witness; divides after 19:14, not at this seam)

boundary_rationale: Hezekiah becomes the sole grammatical subject at 19:14, carrying the letters up and spreading them, וַיַּ֨עַל֙ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה וַיִּפְרְשֵׂ֥הוּ חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה, and that same before-Yahweh staging feeds the prayer's own opening, וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֨ל חִזְקִיָּ֜הוּ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָה֮ וַיֹּאמַר֒ (19:15); לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה at 19:14's end and לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָה֮ mid-verse in 19:15 are the same consonantal phrase under different cantillation, recurring rather than repeating identically, and this consonantal link, together with the prayer's own inclusio (אַתָּה ה֤וּא הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ לְבַדְּךָ֔ in 19:15 answered by אַתָּ֛ה יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים לְבַדֶּֽךָ closing 19:19), is what binds letter-spreading to prayer as one scene. A petuchah keyed to MT 19:14 itself (single-witness) would, read alone, group that verse with the preceding embassy; it is disclosed and read against here because the syntactic chain into the prayer is the stronger, tier-1 signal. The prayer runs from its petition וְעַתָּה֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ הוֹשִׁיעֵ֥נוּ נָ֖א מִיָּד֑וֹ at the head of 19:19 to the recognition clause that closes it, where the setumah (single-witness) corroborates.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Ending the previous unit at 19:14 out of deference to its petuchah fails because that mark is single-witness and weak, while Hezekiah's unbroken subject-chain and the prayer's own answering inclusio are the tier-1 signals that actually carry the letter-spreading act into the prayer.

boundary_rationale: The commission formula וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ יְשַֽׁעְיָ֣הוּ בֶן אָמ֔וֹץ אֶל חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ לֵאמֹ֑ר (19:20) opens Isaiah's reply, and the tag זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה עָלָ֑יו (19:21) marks the taunt's start within that same quotation, since it never receives a sending verb of its own. The taunt is spoken against the Assyrian king, marked by the 2ms suffix on לְךָ֜ in בָּזָ֨ה לְךָ֜ לָעֲגָ֣ה לְךָ֗ (19:21); בְּתוּלַת֙ בַּת צִיּ֔וֹן is the grammatical subject performing that mockery, not the party addressed, and the identical 2ms addressee is carried without a break through חֵרַ֨פְתָּ֙ (19:22), שָׁמַ֤עְתָּ (19:25), and וְשִׁבְתְּךָ֛ (19:27) to the hook-and-bridle image closing the row, וְשַׂמְתִּ֨י חַחִ֜י בְּאַפֶּ֗ךָ וּמִתְגִּי֙ בִּשְׂפָתֶ֔יךָ (19:28). Both addressee and genre shift only at 19:29's 2mp imperatives (זִרְע֧וּ וְקִצְר֛וּ), not at the sign formula's own 2ms לְּךָ֣, which carries the taunt's addressee one clause further; this row's close still sits at 19:28/19:29.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting 19:20 off as its own one-verse commission row and starting the taunt fresh at 19:21 fails because 19:21 introduces its content inside the same quotation 19:20 already opened, without any new sending verb of its own.

boundary_rationale: A waw-joined verbless clause opens this unit, וְזֶה לְּךָ֣ הָא֔וֹת (19:29), whose לְּךָ֣ is the identical 2ms suffix used throughout the taunt and so cannot itself carry the addressee shift; the audience only becomes visibly different at that verse's own plural imperatives, זִרְע֧וּ וְקִצְר֛וּ וְנִטְע֥וּ כְרָמִ֖ים וְאִכְל֥וּ, agricultural instructions presupposing a Judahite community rather than the Assyrian king. A fruit catchword binds the three verses end to end, פִרְיָֽם closing 19:29 answered by פְרִ֖י in 19:30, and 19:30's פְּלֵיטַ֧ת בֵּית יְהוּדָ֛ה anticipates the שְׁאֵרִ֔ית וּפְלֵיטָ֖ה pairing that closes 19:31, קִנְאַ֛ת יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת תַּֽעֲשֶׂה זֹּֽאת. A setumah keyed to 19:31 (single-witness) sits at that close and corroborates, without driving, the edge ahead of the לָכֵ֗ן-marked unit that follows.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 19:21-31 as one uninterrupted oracle fails because the taunt's 2ms address to the Assyrian king cannot be the same referent as the 2mp agricultural imperatives of 19:29, which name no addressee the taunt itself ever supplies.

boundary_rationale: An inferential לָכֵ֗ן opens quoted divine speech about the Assyrian king specifically, לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר (19:32), the messenger-speech frame distinguishing this unit from both the taunt's direct address and the sign's agricultural imperatives to the remnant. Nothing here is narrated in the narrator's own voice: 19:33 closes on the oracle signature נְאֻם יְהוָֽה and 19:34 shifts to first-person divine speech, וְגַנּוֹתִ֛י אֶל הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֖את לְהֽוֹשִׁיעָ֑הּ לְמַֽעֲנִ֔י וּלְמַ֖עַן דָּוִ֥ד עַבְדִּֽי, quoted divine speech that names the Assyrian king in the third person throughout and turns to Yahweh's own 1cs self-reference only at 19:34's וְגַנּוֹתִ֛י, though the frame (כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙) and signature (נְאֻם יְהוָֽה) also name the speaker in the third person. The phrase 'this city' recurs under different cantillation across all three verses, הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את in 19:32, הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֛את in 19:33, הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֖את in 19:34, holding the span together up to its close, immediately before 19:35's own temporal restart, וַיְהִי֮ בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַהוּא֒.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching 19:32-34 to the sign oracle as one continuous unit fails because the לָכֵ֗ן clause reopens quoted speech about the Assyrian king specifically, reverting from the sign's second-person address to the remnant back to a third-person topic inside Yahweh's own words.

boundary_rationale: A fresh temporal marker and subject shift open this closing notice, וַיְהִי֮ בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַהוּא֒ וַיֵּצֵ֣א מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֗ה (19:35), moving from divine speech to narrated fulfillment of the deliverance just promised. It runs through Sennacherib's return and assassination to the succession formula וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אֵֽסַר חַדֹּ֥ן בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו (19:37); here too the tradition places a petuchah (oshb:2Kgs.19.37, petuchah, single-witness), closing the entire Sennacherib complex begun at 18:13. That succession formula is itself the signal of closure, since Kings uses the identical device to end reigns throughout the framework.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding 19:35-37 into the preceding oracle as its fulfillment tail loses because 19:35 restarts the narrative with its own temporal frame and a new grammatical subject, the angel, rather than continuing Yahweh's first-person speech of 19:32-34.

boundary_rationale: A temporal frame distinct from the Sennacherib complex opens this unit, בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם חָלָ֥ה חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ לָמ֑וּת (20:1), introducing the illness Isaiah's oracle and Hezekiah's prayer answer. A samekh keyed to 20:3 falls after that verse's petition and weeping notice close, וַיֵּ֥בְךְּ חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ בְּכִ֥י גָדֽוֹל, immediately before the word reaches Isaiah in 20:4, not mid-prayer as such, and is treated as weak, single-witness corroboration of internal articulation rather than a seam. The clause that actually keeps the sign-request of 20:8-11 inside this same audience, rather than mark or genre labels, is 20:4's own circumstantial construction, וַיְהִ֣י יְשַׁעְיָ֔הוּ לֹ֣א יָצָ֔א, presupposing that Isaiah is still present when the fuller healing word comes; the unit closes on the shadow's reversal, וַיָּ֣שֶׁב אֶת הַצֵּ֗ל בַּֽ֠מַּעֲלוֹת אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָרְדָ֜ה בְּמַעֲל֥וֹת אָחָ֛ז אֲחֹֽרַנִּ֖ית עֶ֥שֶׂר מַעֲלֽוֹת (20:11), after which a petuchah (single-witness) precedes the wholly distinct envoy notice at 20:12.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Separating the sign-act of 20:8-11 from the healing narrative of 20:1-7 fails because 20:4's circumstantial clause keeps Isaiah present at court, so no new arrival or commission formula ever intervenes between Hezekiah's question and Isaiah's answer.

boundary_rationale: A distinct 'at that time' formula opens this scene on a new king and errand, בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֡יא שָׁלַ֡ח בְּרֹאדַ֣ךְ בַּ֠לְאֲדָן ... סְפָרִ֥ים וּמִנְחָ֖ה אֶל חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּ (20:12); the noun סְפָרִ֥ים recurs from 19:14 and 10:1, so the letters are a link back to the Assyrian embassy rather than a contrast with it, and what actually distinguishes this envoy is the וּמִנְחָ֖ה and its Babylonian sender. Isaiah's entrance at 20:14, וַיָּבֹא֙ יְשַֽׁעְיָ֣הוּ הַנָּבִ֔יא אֶל הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּ, is a genuine new-participant arrival using the same arrival device that stands, subordinate to its own temporal frame, as the second clause of 20:1 (וַיָּבֹ֣א אֵ֠לָיו יְשַׁעְיָ֨הוּ בֶן אָמ֜וֹץ הַנָּבִ֗יא) -- there with the pronominal goal and the patronym, here with an explicit 'to the king' phrase (וַיָּבֹא֙ יְשַֽׁעְיָ֣הוּ הַנָּבִ֔יא אֶל הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּ), and Isaiah is truly absent from 20:12-13; no participant-gap denial is defensible here. What keeps 20:14 inside this scene rather than opening a fresh one is that his question, מָ֥ה אָמְר֣וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה וּמֵאַ֨יִן֙ יָבֹ֣אוּ אֵלֶ֔יךָ, anaphorically interrogates 'these men,' the very envoys 20:12-13 just narrated, reusing the arrival formula for a turn inside an already-running audience rather than to open a new one the way 20:1 does. The book strategy's own pre-drafted architecture independently commits ch 20 to three units with 'envoys/oracle 20:12-19' named as one before this row existed, and separately catalogues this exchange as turn-marker territory rather than seam territory; the scene runs unbroken through Hezekiah's closing response, ט֥וֹב דְּבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבַּ֑רְתָּ (20:19), before the regnal source-citation formula at 20:20 marks the true, generically unrelated seam. Unlike 20:8, where 20:4's circumstantial וַיְהִ֣י יְשַׁעְיָ֔הוּ לֹ֣א יָצָ֔א removes any arrival formula and so removes any seam-candidate, 20:14 does supply a genuine arrival formula and is held inside this scene only by the anaphoric force of Isaiah's question.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating Isaiah's interrogation and oracle in 20:14-19 from the envoy visit in 20:12-13 as its own row is the genuinely strongest rival, since Isaiah is truly absent from 20:12-13 and his arrival formula duplicates 20:1's device, but it fails because his opening question names and interrogates the very envoys just narrated, sharing their location and topic without any break, the exact turn-marker configuration this book's strategy declines to treat as a seam.

boundary_rationale: The stock frame וְיֶ֨תֶר דִּבְרֵ֤י חִזְקִיָּ֨הוּ֙ ... הֲלֹא הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה (20:20) opens this close and is structurally unrelated to Isaiah's preceding oracle, though the clause it wraps, וַאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֗ה אֶת הַבְּרֵכָה֙ וְאֶת הַתְּעָלָ֔ה וַיָּבֵ֥א אֶת הַמַּ֖יִם הָעִ֑ירָה, is reign-specific in the way this archival slot ordinarily is elsewhere (13:12, 14:28, 15:15); it is the citation frame itself, not the notice as a whole, that recurs in stock form (with הֲלֹא / הֲלֽוֹא / הִנָּ֣ם orthographic variants) across reigns. The death-and-succession formula completes the row, וַיִּשְׁכַּ֥ב חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ עִם אֲבֹתָ֑יו וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ מְנַשֶּׁ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו (20:21), where the petuchah closing this reign sits (single-witness). This two-verse notice needs no further internal division; its genre break from the preceding dialogue, not any claim about the pool clause's genericness, is what defeats reading it as a mere coda.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating this closing pair as a coda attached to the envoy-oracle scene fails because the citation frame is this book's recurring device for ending any reign, answering nothing the envoy exchange raised, whatever reign-specific material that frame happens to wrap.

boundary_rationale: The row opens on the Judahite-style accession formula, בֶּן שְׁתֵּ֨ים עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה בְמָלְכ֔וֹ (21:1), an age-length-mother notice matching the shape used at most of Judah's other reign-openers (21:19, 22:1, 23:31, 23:36, 24:8, 24:18) rather than every reign-opening in the book, though 8:17 and 16:2 omit the mother's-name element and 18:2 casts the age clause with a finite verb (הָיָ֣ה בְמָלְכ֔וֹ) rather than 21:1's direct construct (מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה בְמָלְכ֔וֹ), since eight northern openers (13:1, 13:10, 14:23, 15:8, 15:17, 15:23, 15:27, 17:1) are bare synchronisms lacking both elements. It closes on the narrator's summary, וְלֹ֖א שָׁמֵ֑עוּ וַיַּתְעֵ֤ם מְנַשֶּׁה֙ לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת אֶת הָרָ֔ע (21:9, 'But they didn’t listen, and Manasseh seduced them to do that which is evil more than the nations did whom Yahweh destroyed before the children of Israel.', WEB), the verse before narration hands over to a quoted speech-report, וַיְדַבֵּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה בְּיַד עֲבָדָ֥יו הַנְּבִיאִ֖ים לֵאמֹֽר (21:10). No parashah mark falls anywhere in this stretch, the nearest standing after MT 20:21 and MT 21:11, so the seam rests entirely on the accession-to-speech-report pairing rather than on the apparatus.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding verses 1-9 together with the oracle into a single eighteen-verse Manasseh frame erases the narration-to-quotation seam only if this book's Commission/messenger-formula category treats 21:10 as one of many equivalent unit-openers; but of its members only 9:1-3 and 19:20 open their own units on this strategy's own architecture (1:3 and 1:15 sit inside the single 1:2-17a arc, and 22:15-17 sits inside this cluster's own row 22:14-20), so the appeal narrows to those two.

boundary_rationale: Direct quoted speech begins with a commission notice, וַיְדַבֵּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה בְּיַד עֲבָדָ֥יו הַנְּבִיאִ֖ים לֵאמֹֽר (21:10), a speech-report rather than the book's Botenformel proper, which instead surfaces within the quotation itself. 21:11 opens that quotation as third-person indictment, יַעַן֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֜ה מְנַשֶּׁ֤ה מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָה֙ ... וַיַּחֲטִ֥א גַֽם אֶת יְהוּדָ֖ה בְּגִלּוּלָֽיו, with no first-person form anywhere in it; the pivot from accusation to sentence falls at 21:12, where לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל introduces the oracle's first first-person verb, הִנְנִי֙ מֵבִ֣יא רָעָ֔ה, which then carries the unit to its final motive clause at 21:15. This indictment-to-sentence shape is the standard two-part structure of a single prophetic judgment oracle governed by one commission notice, not two independently commissioned speeches, and the guilt notice returning to third-person narration in 21:16, וְגַם֩ דָּ֨ם נָקִ֜י שָׁפַ֤ךְ מְנַשֶּׁה֙, stands clearly outside this quoted unit. A petuchah keyed to MT 21:11 (single-witness) lands exactly at that internal pivot; it corroborates where the pivot falls without ever driving a further split.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Dividing this row at the indictment-to-sentence pivot, treating 21:10-11 and 21:12-15 as separate units, is the genuinely strongest rival, since a real person-shift and a Masoretic mark coincide there, but it fails because one commission notice at 21:10 governs the whole quoted speech, and accusation-then-verdict is the ordinary internal shape of a single judgment oracle rather than a seam between two.

boundary_rationale: Narration resumes outside the quoted oracle with the fronted-object bloodshed notice, וְגַם֩ דָּ֨ם נָקִ֜י שָׁפַ֤ךְ מְנַשֶּׁה֙ (21:16), answering back to 21:9's 'led astray' summary. This three-verse unit's own close sits on the archival formula, וְיֶ֨תֶר דִּבְרֵ֤י מְנַשֶּׁה֙ ... הֲלֹא הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים (21:17), paired with the death-burial-succession notice, וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב מְנַשֶּׁה֙ עִם אֲבֹתָ֔יו ... וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אָמ֥וֹן בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו (21:18); that sleeping-with-fathers device closes thirteen reigns in this book (8:24, 10:35, 13:9, 13:13, 14:16, 14:29, 15:7, 15:22, 15:38, 16:20, 20:21, 21:18, 24:6), not every reign, since Amon's own close in the very next row lacks it entirely. The apparatus marks MT 21:18 with a petuchah (single-witness), a weak nod toward the reign boundary standing just before Amon's own opening formula at 21:19.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching these three verses back onto 21:1-9 as a single pre- and post-oracle Manasseh unit fails because it treats the intervening commissioned speech at 21:10 as parenthetical rather than as governing its own quoted unit, a reading the messenger notice does not support.

boundary_rationale: Amon's reign opens with its own accession formula, בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וּשְׁתַּ֤יִם שָׁנָה֙ אָמ֣וֹן בְּמָלְכ֔וֹ (21:19), fresh off Manasseh's closed frame. The unit runs through the conspiracy report, וַיִּקְשְׁר֥וּ עַבְדֵֽי אָמ֖וֹן עָלָ֑יו וַיָּמִ֥יתוּ אֶת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ בְּבֵיתֽוֹ (21:23), and the people's reprisal, וַיַּךְ֙ עַם הָאָ֔רֶץ אֵ֥ת כָּל הַקֹּשְׁרִ֖ים ... וַיַּמְלִ֧יכוּ עַם הָאָ֛רֶץ אֶת יֹאשִׁיָּ֥הוּ (21:24), a pairing no other assassination report in this book carries within its own close (compare the displaced reprisal executed by the successor king at 14:5) rather than at every regicide: Joash's own conspiracy passes straight to succession with no reprisal recorded (MT 12:21-22), Amaziah's killers go unpunished while the people simply enthrone Azariah (14:19-21), and the northern regicides end with the conspirator himself taking the throne (15:10, 15:14, 15:25, 15:30). The row closes on the archival formula, וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י אָמ֖וֹן אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲלֹא הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים (21:25), and the burial-succession notice, וַיִּקְבְֹּ֥ר אֹת֛וֹ בִּקְבֻרָת֖וֹ בְּגַן עֻזָּ֑א וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יֹאשִׁיָּ֥הוּ בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו (21:26), where a petuchah (single-witness) lends faint support to the reign close standing ahead of Josiah's opener at 22:1.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the servants' plot at 21:23 from the people's counter-execution at 21:24 into separate rows would carve one continuous succession event down the middle, against the shared subject chain running unbroken from conspiracy into the succession clause that completes it.

boundary_rationale: Josiah's frame opens with the accession-notice shape shared by his two immediate predecessors, בֶּן שְׁמֹנֶ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ יֹאשִׁיָּ֣הוּ בְמָלְכ֔וֹ (22:1), paired with the first favorable evaluation since Hezekiah, וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הַיָּשָׁ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה ... וְלֹא סָ֖ר יָמִ֥ין וּשְׂמֹֽאול (22:2). Here, unlike at Manasseh's or Amon's openers, the pair really is set off: a petuchah follows MT 22:2 (single-witness) and the date formula opening the book-finding commission, וַיְהִ֗י בִּשְׁמֹנֶ֤ה עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ יֹאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ (22:3), immediately follows. Manasseh's own opener runs straight into plain narrative wayyiqtol with no mark until after MT 21:11, while Amon's opener likewise proceeds unmarked into 21:21 until the apparatus breaks after MT 21:26; the separating force here is thus Josiah-specific rather than a rule this book applies to every accession pair. Nothing internal to 22:1-2 offers any further seam.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging these two verses forward into the book-finding narrative to make one 22:1-13 row fails because it would erase the one convergence of mark and date-formula that genuinely sets this accession-and-evaluation pair off on its own, even though that convergence does not recur at the sibling reign-openers earlier in this same cluster.

boundary_rationale: This second commission opens on its own date formula, וַיְהִ֗י בִּשְׁמֹנֶ֤ה עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ יֹאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ שָׁלַ֣ח הַ֠מֶּלֶךְ אֶת שָׁפָ֨ן (22:3); a petuchah keyed to 22:2 sits just before it (single-witness, the same mark row M8-2Kgs-078 already cites for that juncture), giving this leading edge weak corroboration rather than none. The arc runs through the discovery notice, the reading, and the king's tearing of his clothes to the second commission's own imperative, לְכוּ֩ דִרְשׁ֨וּ אֶת יְהוָ֜ה בַּעֲדִ֣י וּבְעַד הָעָ֗ם (22:13); that imperative is answered not by Shaphan's circle staying in place but by a departure toward a differently named person and quarter at 22:14, so the trailing edge sits exactly where the errand changes destination, and no mark falls anywhere across 22:3-13 itself, the next one standing only after MT 23:30.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The whole 22:3-20 sequence could stand as one arc bound by its own report-inclusio, Shaphan's וַיָּ֥שֶׁב אֶת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ דָּבָ֑ר in 22:9 answered by וַיָּשִׁ֥יבוּ אֶת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ דָּבָֽר in 22:20, and that framing is real, yet it does not erase the arrival shift toward Huldah that this book elsewhere treats as opening a fresh scene.

boundary_rationale: The delegation discharges the king's 22:13 commission by going to a newly named prophetess in a newly named quarter, וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ חִלְקִיָּ֣הוּ הַ֠כֹּהֵן...אֶל חֻלְדָּ֨ה הַנְּבִיאָ֜ה...וְהִ֛יא יֹשֶׁ֥בֶת בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בַּמִּשְׁנֶ֑ה (2Kgs.22.14); the closest formal analogue, Hazael's errand to Elisha at 2Kgs.8.8-9 (וְלֵ֕ךְ לִקְרַ֖את אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְדָרַשְׁתָּ֨ אֶת יְהוָ֤ה מֵֽאוֹתוֹ֙ ... וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ חֲזָאֵל֮ לִקְרָאתוֹ֒), keeps its own command and its own going inside one continuous scene, so the going-verb alone cannot carry this row's separation. What actually distinguishes 22:14 is that the errand lands on a person and a location neither named nor staged anywhere earlier in the chapter, unlike Hazael's errand, which is discharged back onto a 'man of God' already on stage from the surrounding Elisha material; and the scene closes on its own report-back formula, וַיָּשִׁ֥יבוּ אֶת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ דָּבָֽר (2Kgs.22.20), which the Hazael errand also supplies at 8:14 (וַיָּבֹא֙ אֶל אֲדֹנָ֔יו וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ); what actually distinguishes 22:14-20 is the errand landing on a person and place named nowhere earlier in the chapter, not the mere presence of a report-back. Huldah's two-part answer turns on its own internal address shift at וְאֶל מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֗ה הַשֹּׁלֵ֤חַ אֶתְכֶם֙ (2Kgs.22.18, 'but to the king of Judah who sent you'), yet nothing there reopens the scene, so that turn stays inside this single row, which ends before 23:1 opens its own assembly formula.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The strongest rival reads Hazael's own errand at 8:8-9 as the closer analogue, since both discharge a king's commission with the same going-verb inside continuous action, but it does not survive the contrast in addressee-novelty and in the closing report formula that 22:14-20 supplies and 8:8-9 does not.

boundary_rationale: The king's summons opens this unit, וַיִּשְׁלַ֖ח הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיַּאַסְפ֣וּ אֵלָ֔יו כָּל זִקְנֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה וִירוּשָׁלִָֽם (2Kgs.23.1), an assembly formula answering Huldah's report with a far larger cast than the prior scene's five named men. It closes on the people's ratification, וַיַּעֲמֹ֥ד כָּל הָעָ֖ם בַּבְּרִֽית (2Kgs.23.3, 'and all the people stood in the covenant'), just before the king's fresh instruction to Hilkiah at 23:4 opens the purge catalogue with a different verb and a different object entirely. Neither pe nor samekh corroborates either edge here, but the assembly-open, ratification-close pairing needs no such support to stand.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Absorbing 23:1-3 into the purge catalogue as its preamble would treat the covenant scene as mere throat-clearing before the reforms, but the covenant's own ratification clause gives this scene a closure the catalogue's opening command simply does not share.

boundary_rationale: The king's command to Hilkiah, the second-order priests, and the threshold-keepers, וַיְצַ֣ו הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ אֶת חִלְקִיָּהוּ֩ הַכֹּהֵ֨ן הַגָּד֜וֹל...לְהוֹצִיא֙ מֵהֵיכַ֣ל יְהוָ֔ה (2Kgs.23.4), opens this first movement, whose acting scene stays inside Jerusalem and Judah even though its own closing clause already reaches toward the next movement's destination, וְנָשָׂ֥א אֶת עֲפָרָ֖ם בֵּֽית אֵֽל ('and he carried their ashes to Bethel'), an anticipation of what 23:15 will do at length rather than a counter-example to the territorial contrast. Two internal turns, וְאֶֽת הַֽמִּזְבְּח֡וֹת...נָתַ֣ץ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ (23:12) and וְֽאֶת הַבָּמ֞וֹת...טִמֵּ֖א הַמֶּֽלֶךְ (23:13), share the same disjunctive fronted-object-and-delayed-verb shape that 23:15 and 23:19 use, but neither carries the additive גַם particle that actually marks this register's movement-openers, and neither opens any territory beyond Jerusalem and Judah, so the register's tripartite division survives: what distinguishes a movement-opener from an ordinary internal turn is גַם, not fronting by itself. The movement runs through its own summary close, וְשִׁבַּר֙ אֶת הַמַּצֵּב֔וֹת וַיִּכְרֹ֖ת אֶת הָאֲשֵׁרִ֑ים וַיְמַלֵּ֥א אֶת מְקוֹמָ֖ם עַצְמ֥וֹת אָדָֽם (2Kgs.23.14), before 23:15's own גַם-headed clause reopens the register at a place outside Judah. Restated conjunctively: a movement-opener carries גַם and names territory outside Judah/Jerusalem; 23:24's own clause stays inside that territory (בְּאֶ֤רֶץ יְהוּדָה֙ וּבִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם) and so fails the second half of the test even while sharing the particle.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting this eleven-verse stretch at 23:12 or 23:13, where the same fronted-object-and-delayed-verb shape as 23:15/23:19 recurs, is the genuinely closest rival, but it fails once גַם is isolated as the actual movement-marking particle: neither verse opens with it, and neither reaches beyond Jerusalem and Judah's own territory.

boundary_rationale: The register's second movement opens on its own location-shift marker, וְגַ֨ם אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּ֜חַ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּבֵֽית אֵ֗ל (2Kgs.23.15, 'moreover, the altar that was at Bethel'), echoing the same construction that reopens the register a third time at 23:19. Its center carries the fulfillment notice כִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר קָרָא֙ אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים (2Kgs.23.16), a cross-reference recognizable from the unnamed man of God's Bethel oracle (a chain reaching into 1Kgs 13, noted here only as background observation, not as a source consulted). The unit closes with the bones left undisturbed, וַֽיְמַלְּטוּ֙ עַצְמֹתָ֔יו אֵ֚ת עַצְמ֣וֹת הַנָּבִ֔יא אֲשֶׁר בָּ֖א מִשֹּׁמְרֽוֹן (2Kgs.23.18), before the register turns to Samaria's cities in the next clause.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Lumping the Bethel movement together with the preceding Jerusalem-and-Judah verses into one long purge row would erase the very repeated location-shift device that gives this register its only legitimate internal seams.

boundary_rationale: A second גַם-headed clause reopens the register for the northern cities, וְגַם֩ אֶת כָּל בָּתֵּ֨י הַבָּמ֜וֹת אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּעָרֵ֣י שֹׁמְר֗וֹן (2Kgs.23.19), sharing its fronted-object-and-locative-relative shape with 23:15's own opener rather than with 23:4, which opens instead on the command formula וַיְצַ֣ו הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ; the three verses are functional parallels, each launching a movement, but only 23:15 and 23:19 share the same grammatical construction. This movement stays brief because its comparison clause, וַיַּ֣עַשׂ לָהֶ֔ם כְּכָל הַֽמַּעֲשִׂ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה בְּבֵֽית אֵֽל ('he did to them according to all the deeds he had done at Bethel'), concerns the fate of the shrine-houses, not a slaughter that never occurs at Bethel; the priest-slaughter narrated at וַ֠יִּזְבַּח אֶת כָּל כֹּהֲנֵ֨י הַבָּמ֤וֹת (23:20) is fresh action carried by its own verbs rather than a back-reference. This movement, and with it the whole register, closes on the travel notice returning the king to base, וַיָּ֖שָׁב יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם (2Kgs.23.20), immediately before a new topic opens with its own command verb at 23:21.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 23:19-20 as a mere coda folded into the Bethel row would deny this shortest movement the marked status its גַם-headed opener genuinely shares with 23:15, even though the movement's brevity comes from comparing the shrine-houses' fate rather than from repeating any slaughter.

boundary_rationale: A fresh command formula opens this unit, וַיְצַ֤ו הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֶת כָּל הָעָ֣ם לֵאמֹ֔ר עֲשׂ֣וּ פֶ֔סַח לַֽיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֑ם (2Kgs.23.21), distinct in addressee (all the people, not priests) and subject matter (a festival, not idol removal) from the purge register just closed. The evaluative claim כִּ֣י לֹ֤א נַֽעֲשָׂה֙ כַּפֶּ֣סַח הַזֶּ֔ה מִימֵי֙ הַשֹּׁ֣פְטִ֔ים (2Kgs.23.22) is reported here as this text's own stated claim about the occasion, not verified here against every other Passover mention in the corpus, and the date-anchored close at 23:23 finishes the unit before 23:24 shifts to a different object list without a comparable command verb.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching 23:21-23 onto the purge catalogue as its final movement would overlook that the command verb here addresses the whole people rather than priests and threshold-keepers, and that no location marker of the register's kind introduces it.

boundary_rationale: This is the part's genuinely soft stretch. Verse 24 opens with וְגַ֣ם ('and also'), the same particle marking the register's movement-openers at 23:15 and 23:19, and it in fact reuses their full construction: fronted objects, a locative relative, אֲשֶׁ֤ר נִרְאוּ֙ בְּאֶ֤רֶץ יְהוּדָה֙ וּבִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם, resumed by its own main-clause qatal, בִּעֵ֖ר יֹֽאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ, answering 23:19's הֵסִ֖יר יֹֽאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ, so what actually distinguishes it from a fresh movement is territorial scope, not construction: no new place is named. A real tier-1 tie does bind the wrath notice to what precedes it: 23:25's claim that no king before Josiah אֲשֶׁר שָׁ֤ב אֶל יְהוָה֙ ('who turned to Yahweh') is answered in flat antithesis by 23:26's אַ֣ךְ לֹֽא שָׁ֣ב יְהוָ֗ה ('nevertheless Yahweh did not turn'), the same root, שָׁ֤ב answered by שָׁ֣ב, negated across the seam, which keeps the wrath notice bound to the reform summary rather than floating free toward the death notice's own source-citation formula opening at 23:28. Nothing marks a fresh unit anywhere between 23:24 and 23:27, and no parashah mark falls in this stretch either, so this four-verse span stays whole on the strength of that repeated root. Unlike 23:15's אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּבֵֽית אֵ֗ל and 23:19's אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּעָרֵ֣י שֹׁמְר֗וֹן, both verbless, this relative is a finite niphal.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching 23:26-27 to the death-and-burial unit that follows, on the theory that the unturned wrath foreshadows Josiah's coming death, remains arguable from content alone, but the antithesis linking 23:25 to 23:26 gives this stretch an internal tie the following death notice does not share, so keeping the wrath notice here has better grounding than moving it forward.

boundary_rationale: The standard source-citation formula opens this close, וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י יֹאשִׁיָּ֖הוּ וְכָל אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה...הֲלֹא הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים (2Kgs.23.28), running through Necoh's campaign and Josiah's death at Megiddo to the burial-and-anointing notice, וַיִּקַּ֣ח עַם הָאָ֗רֶץ אֶת יְהֽוֹאָחָז֙...וַיַּמְלִ֥יכוּ אֹת֖וֹ תַּ֥חַת אָבִֽיו (2Kgs.23.30). The people-of-the-land enthronement clause closing this verse belongs to the outgoing king's own close, not to any incoming accession template: a book-wide search for the verse-initial age-plus-name accession pattern returns fifteen hits (8:17, 8:26, 12:1 [MT] = 11:21 [WEB], 14:2, 15:2, 15:33, 16:2, 18:2, 21:1, 21:19, 22:1, 23:31, 23:36, 24:8, 24:18), and 23:30b matches none of them, while the closing collocation תַּ֥חַת אָבִֽיו itself occurs only twice in the whole book, here and at 2Kgs.14.21 (וַיַּמְלִ֣כוּ אֹת֔וֹ תַּ֖חַת אָבִ֥יו אֲמַצְיָֽהוּ), where it likewise sits inside Amaziah's own death-and-succession sequence ahead of Azariah's fresh template at 15:1-2, and parallels the still-closer Amon-to-Josiah transition at 21:24 (וַיַּמְלִ֧יכוּ עַם הָאָ֛רֶץ אֶת יֹאשִׁיָּ֥הוּ בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו), which likewise precedes Amon's own source-citation close at 21:25 rather than opening Josiah's template at 22:1. The parashah apparatus marks MT 23:30 itself with a petuchah break (oshb:2Kgs.23.30, single-witness), corroborating this row's own close, and Jehoahaz's fresh accession formula opens cleanly at 23:31 with nothing of 23:30 pulling loose from it. The two-hit count is itself consonantal: 23:30 reads תַּ֥חַת אָבִֽיו while 14:21 reads תַּ֖חַת אָבִ֥יו, differing in accentuation on both words.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Peeling 23:30b off as the true opening half-verse of Jehoahaz's reign looked tempting on a first pass, since it names the new king, but it is decisively defeated by the book's own convention: the people-of-the-land enthronement clause is predecessor-close material everywhere else it occurs (14:21, 21:24), never a reign-opener, so the literary seam and the administrative part-boundary at 23:30 in fact agree rather than conflict.

literature_type_guess: regnal_framework_notice (accession frame with foreign deposition and tribute)
boundary_rationale: Jehoahaz's reign begins on its own age-at-accession template, בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְשָׁלֹ֤שׁ שָׁנָה֙ יְהוֹאָחָ֣ז בְּמָלְכ֔וֹ (oshb:2Kgs.23.31), immediately after the people-of-the-land anointing notice at 23:30 (oshb:2Kgs.23.30 — single-witness, a pe stands there in MT). The block runs through Necoh's arrest-and-fine notice, וַיַּאַסְרֵהוּ֩ פַרְעֹ֨ה נְכֹ֤ה בְרִבְלָה֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ חֲמָ֔ת במלך מִמְּלֹ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַיִּתֶּן עֹ֨נֶשׁ֙ עַל הָאָ֔רֶץ (oshb:2Kgs.23.33 — במלך is the ketiv and מִמְּלֹ֖ךְ its qere, printed here as the source prints them so the pair is not misread as a doubled word), through Jehoiakim's installation at 23:34, וַיַּמְלֵךְ֩ פַּרְעֹ֨ה נְכֹ֜ה אֶת אֶלְיָקִ֣ים בֶּן יֹאשִׁיָּ֗הוּ תַּ֚חַת יֹאשִׁיָּ֣הוּ אָבִ֔יו וַיַּסֵּ֥ב אֶת שְׁמ֖וֹ יְהוֹיָקִ֑ים, and the further fronted-object qatal reporting Jehoahaz's removal, וְאֶת יְהוֹאָחָ֣ז לָקָ֔ח, Necoh still its subject, and one clause inside this stretch does interrupt the Necoh-as-subject chain: 23:35 opens וְהַכֶּ֣סֶף וְהַזָּהָ֗ב נָתַ֤ן יְהוֹיָקִים֙ לְפַרְעֹ֔ה, a disjunctive fronted-double-object qatal whose subject is now the newly installed king rather than Necoh, the only such subject-change in the span. That disjunction does not reopen a row, since the silver and gold it reports directly answer the fine just imposed, מֵאָ֥ה כִכַּר כֶּ֖סֶף וְכִכַּ֥ר זָהָֽב (23:33), so 23:35 closes the arrest-and-tribute sequence rather than opening anything new; the block finishes there (oshb:2Kgs.23.35 — single-witness, MT places a samekh too), before Jehoiakim's contrasting template, בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְחָמֵ֤שׁ שָׁנָ֨ה יְהוֹיָקִ֣ים בְּמָלְכ֔וֹ (oshb:2Kgs.23.36), launches the next reign.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The most serious rival splits off 23:35 as its own row, since Jehoiakim's naming there is a genuine disjunctive subject-change unique in the span, but the fine-to-payment link back to 23:33 makes 23:35 a closing notice rather than a fresh opening.

boundary_rationale: Jehoiakim's own accession pattern, בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְחָמֵ֤שׁ שָׁנָ֨ה יְהוֹיָקִ֣ים בְּמָלְכ֔וֹ (oshb:2Kgs.23.36), opens a unit the modern chapter break artificially cuts away from the annal that depends on it. What follows genuinely includes one classed opening device: 24:1's advent notice, בְּיָמָ֣יו עָלָ֔ה נְבֻכַדְנֶאצַּ֖ר מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֑ל, is exactly the campaign-muster/siege-formula type this book's own device matrix files as an opener elsewhere, so this row concedes 24:1 is not a bare narrator's aside. It nonetheless stays inside Jehoiakim's own frame rather than launching a fourth row: the strategy's own architecture divides chapter 24 into three frames only, matching this row plus the Jehoiachin frame (090) and the Zedekiah frame (091), with no fourth 24:1-2 unit anywhere in that count, and its own expected-low-confidence list separately names '24:1-7 Jehoiakim compressed annal' as one pre-anticipated unit rather than a splittable pair. Unlike the genuine campaign-musters this book reports at length (the multi-verse Moab campaign of 3:5-7, itself dated only by the loose בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא), 24:1's two verses carry no described muster (contrast 3:6's וַיִּפְקֹ֖ד אֶת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל); they compress advent and revolt into a report that immediately answers itself in the fulfillment notice closing 24:2, כִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֔ר בְּיַ֖ד עֲבָדָ֥יו הַנְּבִיאִֽים, itself one clause among the paratactic run of notices — the raiding bands, the source citation at 24:5 (וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י יְהוֹיָקִ֖ים וְכָל אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲלֹא הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה), the death-and-succession clause at 24:6 (וַיִּשְׁכַּ֥ב יְהוֹיָקִ֖ים עִם אֲבֹתָ֑יו וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יְהוֹיָכִ֥ין בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו), and the Egypt aside at 24:7 (וְלֹֽא הֹסִ֥יף עוֹד֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם לָצֵ֖את מֵֽאַרְצ֑וֹ כִּֽי לָקַ֞ח מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֗ל מִנַּ֤חַל מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ עַד נְהַר פְּרָ֔ת כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיְתָ֖ה לְמֶ֥לֶךְ מִצְרָֽיִם, MT sets a pe there, single-witness) — that only Jehoiachin's own age-formula, יְהוֹיָכִ֣ין בְּמָלְכ֔וֹ, closes at 24:8.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A genuine rival carves out 24:1-2 as its own campaign-muster-and-fulfillment row, since the strategy's device matrix really does class 24:1 that way, but 24:1's own fronted-temporal-plus-qatal frame, בְּיָמָ֣יו עָלָ֔ה, recurs at 24:10's בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔יא עלה עָל֗וּ as an internal reign-frame notice rather than a fresh opener, which is the textual ground the strategy's three-frame count and compressed-annal label only corroborate.

literature_type_guess: regnal_framework_notice (accession-and-evaluation frame closed by a rebellion hinge)
boundary_rationale: Zedekiah's own accession template, בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְאַחַ֤ת שָׁנָה֙ צִדְקִיָּ֣הוּ בְמָלְכ֔וֹ (oshb:2Kgs.24.18), opens this short notice, which winds down on the rebellion notice וַיִּמְרֹ֥ד צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ בְּמֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶֽל (oshb:2Kgs.24.20 — a samekh follows this verse in MT, single-witness). strongest_rejected_alternative: Pulling 25:1 into this reign-frame because the rebellion causally triggers the siege loses since a full year-month-day date formula always opens its own unit elsewhere in this stretch, never merely continuing a prior notice's causal clause.

boundary_rationale: The full date formula וַיְהִי֩ בִשְׁנַ֨ת הַתְּשִׁיעִ֜ית לְמָלְכ֗וֹ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָעֲשִׂירִי֮ בֶּעָשׂ֣וֹר לַחֹדֶשׁ֒ (oshb:2Kgs.25.1) opens the siege; a second internal date, בְּתִשְׁעָ֣ה לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ וַיֶּחֱזַ֥ק הָרָעָ֖ב בָּעִ֑יר (oshb:2Kgs.25.3), marks the famine's worsening rather than a fresh unit. Corroboration there stays weak; the real contrast driving the boundary is the wholly separate date formula that reopens at 25:8, naming a different regnal year and a different named agent for the city's physical destruction.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 25:1-17 as one undivided fall-of-Jerusalem complex loses because 25:8 restarts the date-formula device with Nebuchadnezzar's nineteenth year and introduces Nebuzaradan as an entirely new agent, exactly the contrast this date-articulated sequence uses to mark a fresh unit.

literature_type_guess: destruction_narrative (burning, wall demolition, and remnant deportation notice)
boundary_rationale: Nebuzaradan's arrival under its own date formula, וּבַחֹ֤דֶשׁ הַֽחֲמִישִׁי֙ בְּשִׁבְעָ֣ה לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ הִ֗יא שְׁנַת֙ תְּשַֽׁע עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ נְבֻכַדְנֶאצַּ֣ר מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶ֑ל בָּ֞א נְבוּזַרְאֲדָ֧ן רַב טַבָּחִ֛ים עֶ֥בֶד מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם (oshb:2Kgs.25.8), opens the unit, and Nebuzaradan, named or carried by his title, remains the continuing acting agent through burning, וַיִּשְׂרֹ֥ף אֶת בֵּית יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:2Kgs.25.9, this span's only genuinely verb-initial clause); wall-breaking, וְאֶת חוֹמֹ֥ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם סָבִ֑יב נָֽתְצוּ֙ (oshb:2Kgs.25.10, object fronted ahead of its verb); deportation of the remainder, וְאֵת֩ יֶ֨תֶר הָעָ֜ם הַנִּשְׁאָרִ֣ים בָּעִ֗יר...הֶגְלָ֕ה נְבוּזַרְאֲדָ֖ן (oshb:2Kgs.25.11, likewise object-fronted); and the poor left as vinedressers and plowmen, וּמִדַּלַּ֣ת הָאָ֔רֶץ הִשְׁאִ֖יר רַב טַבָּחִ֑ים (oshb:2Kgs.25.12, fronting a prepositional phrase). Only 25:9 is verb-initial; the other three front an object or a prepositional phrase before their verb, so the edge at 25:13 cannot rest on a verb-initial/object-fronted contrast, since that word-order feature already appears inside 25:8-12 itself. What actually divides 25:8-12 from 25:13-17 is not agent continuity, which in fact straddles the edge: 25:10's army-subject נָֽתְצוּ֙ כָּל חֵ֣יל כַּשְׂדִּ֔ים, 25:13's שִׁבְּר֣וּ כַשְׂדִּ֑ים, and 25:15's לָקַ֖ח רַב טַבָּחִֽים each carry a finite verb on their own side of the seam. The real discriminator is what those verbs act upon. Across 25:8-12 the finite actions bear down on the city and its population -- the burning of וַיִּשְׂרֹ֥ף אֶת בֵּית יְהוָ֖ה (25:9), the wall-breaking of 25:10, and the deportation of the remnant and the poor at 25:11-12 -- whereas 25:13-17 catalogues temple furnishings of bronze, gold, and silver (pillars, sea, stands, pots, shovels, snuffers, bowls, censers, basins), ending in the measurement idiom of 25:16-17 (הָעַמּוּדִ֣ים שְׁנַ֗יִם...; שְׁמֹנֶה֩ עֶשְׂרֵ֨ה אַמָּ֜ה קוֹמַ֣ת הָעַמּ֣וּד...), a construction never reached in 25:8-12. literature_type_guess: destruction_register (temple bronze, gold, and silver vessel inventory)
boundary_rationale: The register opens on a fronted direct object rather than a verb, וְאֶת עַמּוּדֵ֨י הַנְּחֹ֜שֶׁת אֲשֶׁ֣ר בֵּית יְהוָ֗ה וְֽאֶת הַמְּכֹנ֞וֹת וְאֶת יָ֧ם הַנְּחֹ֛שֶׁת (oshb:2Kgs.25.13), and the same accusative-marked chain continues through the itemized list of 25:14, וְאֶת הַסִּירֹ֨ת וְאֶת הַיָּעִ֜ים וְאֶת הַֽמְזַמְּר֣וֹת וְאֶת הַכַּפּ֗וֹת (oshb:2Kgs.25.14); this fronting is not itself register-diagnostic across the book, since verse-initial waw-plus-et occurs at fifteen verses total, including 24:16, 25:7, 25:10, and 25:11, all inside ordinary narrative this cluster keeps un-registered, so the register's real marker is content, not syntax alone. 25:16-17 shift construction again, into two distinct constructions: 25:16 fronts a dislocated topic (הָעַמּוּדִ֣ים שְׁנַ֗יִם הַיָּ֤ם הָֽאֶחָד֙ וְהַמְּכֹנ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂ֥ה שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה לְבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה...) resumed by its own negated predicate (לֹא הָיָ֣ה מִשְׁקָ֔ל...) (oshb:2Kgs.25.16), and 25:17 gives a genuinely verbless measurement clause (שְׁמֹנֶה֩ עֶשְׂרֵ֨ה אַמָּ֜ה קוֹמַ֣ת הָעַמּ֣וּד הָאֶחָ֗ד) (oshb:2Kgs.25.17), neither carrying an accusative marker, a measurement idiom echoing the 1Kgs 7 bronze-furnishings catalogue as a cross-book form-parallel, noted here only as metadata, never as in-book evidence. What genuinely shifts is the object of the verbs. 25:8-12 reports blows struck against the city and against those still living in it -- וַיִּשְׂרֹ֥ף אֶת בֵּית יְהוָ֖ה (25:9), the wall-breaking notice at 25:10, and the exile of the remaining populace, poor included, at 25:11-12 -- while 25:13-17 turns to an inventory of the temple's bronze, gold, and silver vessels: the paired pillars and the sea alongside the stands and the smaller cultic pieces (pots, shovels, snuffers, bowls, censers, basins), closed out by the measurement clauses of 25:16-17 (הָעַמּוּדִ֣ים שְׁנַ֗יִם...; שְׁמֹנֶה֩ עֶשְׂרֵ֨ה אַמָּ֜ה קוֹמַ֣ת הָעַמּ֣וּד...), a form 25:8-12 nowhere takes. Only at 25:18 does the register yield back to a human object, in the renewed verb-initial notice וַיִּקַּ֣ח רַב טַבָּחִ֗ים אֶת... (oshb:2Kgs.25.18), which returns the narrative from objects to a roster of persons.

literature_type_guess: execution_roster (named officials seized and put to death at Riblah)
boundary_rationale: The roster names the chief priest first, וַיִּקַּ֣ח רַב טַבָּחִ֗ים אֶת שְׂרָיָה֙ כֹּהֵ֣ן הָרֹ֔אשׁ וְאֶת צְפַנְיָ֖הוּ כֹּהֵ֣ן מִשְׁנֶ֑ה וְאֶת שְׁלֹ֖שֶׁת שֹׁמְרֵ֥י הַסַּֽף (oshb:2Kgs.25.18), then grades downward through officers, courtiers, a scribe, and וְשִׁשִּׁ֥ים אִישׁ֙ מֵעַ֣ם הָאָ֔רֶץ הַֽנִּמְצְאִ֖ים בָּעִֽיר (oshb:2Kgs.25.19), before the transport formula וַיֹּ֧לֶךְ אֹתָ֛ם עַל מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל רִבְלָֽתָה (oshb:2Kgs.25.20) and the execution notice וַיַּ֣ךְ אֹתָם֩ מֶ֨לֶךְ בָּבֶ֧ל וַיְמִיתֵ֛ם בְּרִבְלָ֖ה בְּאֶ֣רֶץ חֲמָ֑ת וַיִּ֥גֶל יְהוּדָ֖ה מֵעַ֥ל אַדְמָתֽוֹ (oshb:2Kgs.25.21), whose closing clause, 'Judah was carried away captive out of his land,' summarizes and closes the fall-and-execution sequence, though no matching bracket phrase opens the roster to pair with it, so this closural force is better named a summarizing notice than an inclusio, a label this row withdraws for lack of the paired opening the term requires. literature_type_guess: governorship_episode (appointment, oath, assassination, and flight — compressed)
boundary_rationale: The episode opens with Gedaliah's appointment, וְהָעָ֗ם הַנִּשְׁאָר֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ יְהוּדָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִשְׁאִ֔יר נְבֽוּכַדְנֶאצַּ֖ר מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֑ל וַיַּפְקֵ֣ד עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם אֶת גְּדַלְיָ֖הוּ בֶּן אֲחִיקָ֥ם בֶּן שָׁפָֽן (oshb:2Kgs.25.22), and this revision concedes at the outset three claims the earlier draft got wrong: 25:25 does open with a date-shaped clause, וַיְהִ֣י בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗י, immediately naming the royal-seed conspirator, בָּ֣א יִשְׁמָעֵ֣אל בֶּן נְ֠תַנְיָה בֶּן אֱלִ֨ישָׁמָ֜ע מִזֶּ֣רַע הַמְּלוּכָ֗ה; 25:26 does end in a location change, וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ מִצְרָ֑יִם ('and they came to Egypt'); and the Mizpah setting is not continuous from the start, since 25:22 names no place at all and הַמִּצְפָּ֑ה first appears only at 25:23, וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ אֶל גְּדַלְיָ֖הוּ הַמִּצְפָּ֑ה. None of that, however, makes 25:25 a genuine tier-1 opener on this book's own terms: its date gives a month with no year and no reign anchor, unlike the full year-month-day (or exile-year-month-day) triads that open 25:1 (וַיְהִי֩ בִשְׁנַ֨ת הַתְּשִׁיעִ֜ית לְמָלְכ֗וֹ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָעֲשִׂירִי֮), 25:8, and 25:27, the same full-versus-partial distinction row M8-2Kgs-092 already applies to 25:3's day-only date, בְּתִשְׁעָ֣ה לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ, which stays internal to its own siege narrative rather than opening a rival unit. The over_split_risk_check does list '25:1, 25:8, 25:25, 25:27' together as chapter 25's genuine seams, a listing this row does not silently contradict but reads as the coarser survey that predates the finer full/partial-date test applied consistently elsewhere in this fall sequence; once that test is run, 25:25 groups with 25:3 as an internal date rather than with 25:1/25:8/25:27 as a unit-opener. Ishmael himself never receives an accession or installation formula of the kind this book uses to mark a change of ruling agent, and the Egypt departure at 25:26 reads as this episode's own outcome, the flight its assassination provokes, rather than as a fresh scene equivalent to Nebuchadnezzar's or Nebuzaradan's arrivals. On these narrower, corrected grounds the five verses stay one compressed governorship arc, closed only where 25:27's full date formula and new regnal agent, Evil-merodach, actually reopen the frame; the internal pe (25:22) and samekh (25:24), plus the pe at 25:26 (which falls at this row's own closing edge rather than inside it), remain weak, single-witness corroboration under the marks-never-drivers rule. Ishmael himself is not new at 25:25: he is already named among the officers who came to Gedaliah, at 25:23's וְיִשְׁמָעֵ֣אל בֶּן נְתַנְיָ֡ה, a positive ground for keeping 25:22-26 whole.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A split at 25:25, backed by its own date formula, its newly named royal-lineage figure, and surface support from the over_split_risk_check's 'genuine seams' listing, is the most tempting alternative, yet it fails the same full-versus-partial date test that keeps 25:3 internal to its own unit, since 25:25 supplies a month with no regnal year to anchor it.

literature_type_guess: release_notice (exile-era elevation of the suspended Davidic king)
boundary_rationale: The closing unit opens on a fully articulated exile-era date formula naming Jehoiachin's thirty-seventh captive year and Evil-merodach's own accession year, וַיְהִי֩ בִשְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים וָשֶׁ֜בַע שָׁנָ֗ה לְגָלוּת֙ יְהוֹיָכִ֣ין מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה בִּשְׁנֵ֤ים עָשָׂר֙ חֹ֔דֶשׁ בְּעֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְשִׁבְעָ֖ה לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ נָשָׂ֡א אֱוִ֣יל מְרֹדַךְ֩ מֶ֨לֶךְ בָּבֶ֜ל בִּשְׁנַ֣ת מָלְכ֗וֹ אֶת רֹ֛אשׁ יְהוֹיָכִ֥ין מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֖ה מִבֵּ֥ית כֶּֽלֶא (oshb:2Kgs.25.27), an elevation idiom ('lifted the head of...out of the prison-house') wholly distinct from anything in the Gedaliah episode it follows, whose own opener at 25:22, וְהָעָ֗ם הַנִּשְׁאָר֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ יְהוּדָ֔ה, carries no date at all. This narrows rather than repeats the earlier claim that 25:27 opens the same kind of scene-and-agent shift found at every unit in this sequence: the wyhy-plus-date frame itself recurs unit-internally at 25:25 (וַיְהִ֣י בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗י), so the form alone does not discriminate a seam from internal articulation, and what actually carries this opening is the newly named Babylonian king, אֱוִ֣יל מְרֹדַךְ֩, a name occurring nowhere else in the book, together with the relocation to Babylon and the head-lifting release idiom. The unit continues through the throne-elevation formula וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ טֹב֑וֹת וַיִּתֵּן֙ אֶת כִּסְא֔וֹ מֵעַ֗ל כִּסֵּ֧א הַמְּלָכִ֛ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ בְּבָבֶֽל (oshb:2Kgs.25.28) and the perpetual-table notice of 25:29, closing the book on the repeated allowance formula, וַאֲרֻחָת֗וֹ אֲרֻחַ֨ת תָּמִ֧יד נִתְּנָה לּ֛וֹ מֵאֵ֥ת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ דְּבַר י֣וֹם בְּיוֹמ֑וֹ כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽו (oshb:2Kgs.25.30). That final clause is a fronted-subject, niphal-passive construction distinct from 25:28's wayyiqtol and 25:29's weqatal forms, and it is named here rather than passed over: it does not open a fresh seam, because its own תָּמִ֧יד answers 25:29's תָּמִ֛יד לְפָנָ֖יו, and its defective verse-final כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽו answers 25:29's fuller כָּל יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽיו, a catchword repetition binding 25:30 to 25:29 as annalistic summary rather than as a new beginning. The far edge is simply the corpus boundary; the Jer 52:31-34 synoptic parallel is noted only as cross-book metadata, never as evidence for this seam.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 25:27-30 as a coda attached to the Gedaliah unit gains real plausibility from the shared wyhy-plus-date opening form both units use, but it fails once the newly named Babylonian king, the relocation to Babylon, and the head-lifting idiom are isolated as what actually distinguishes an opening use of that form from 25:25's internal one.
